title: Skateboarding Without Limits | PlayLA's Adaptive Skateboarding Program
description:
Skateboarding has no limits—and neither do the people discovering just how far they can go. 🛹💙

Through the PlayLA initiative, the City of Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks' Ability Skateboarding and Action Sports program is making skateboarding accessible to participants of all ages and abilities. Whether someone is blind, deaf, uses a wheelchair, or is stepping onto a skateboard for the first time, the program provides the equipment, instruction, and encouragement needed to build confidence in a supportive environment.

Featured in this segment is Coco Atama, also known as Blind Thrasher, who describes himself as the world's only blind and autistic professional skateboarder.

From skateboards and protective gear to adaptive equipment and one-on-one coaching, participants simply need to show up. 

Learn more about PlayLA Youth and Adaptive Youth Sports Program offered by the City of Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks at https://recreation.parks.lacity.gov/

Un mensaje importante del DPSS sobre el cierre del gobierno federal
description:
Si recibes beneficios de CalFresh, probablemente haz oído hablar del cierre actual del gobierno federal y su impacto en sus beneficios de CalFresh.

Esto es lo que necesitas saber:
• El cierre significa que el gobierno federal no autorizará los beneficios de CalFresh para el mes de noviembre de 2025.
• Una vez que finalice el cierre, se emitirán beneficios a aquellos que fueron elegibles en el mes de noviembre.
• Si su reporte SAR7 de CalFresh o renovación anual vence durante el cierre, DEBE completarlos a tiempo para seguir siendo elegible y poder continuar recibiendo sus beneficios una vez que finalice el cierre.
Te invitamos a visitar tu banco de alimentos local y a contactarte con las organizaciones locales de ayuda mutua para obtener ayuda durante estos momentos difíciles.

Para obtener una lista de ubicaciones, visita LAFoodBank.org o llame al 211 o visita www.211.org.

San Diego Fire Chief Reflects on the Integration of the Fire Department
description:
This Black History Month, San Diego's Fire Chief Robert Logan reflects on the trailblazing legacy of Alwin Benjamin Holman.

Before Holman integrated Fire Station 14 in North Park in 1951, all Black firefighters in San Diego were segregated in Fire Station 19 in Mountain View. Holman later became San Diego’s first Black Deputy Fire Chief, serving 32 years.

Chief Logan credits Holman for opening doors that made his own journey possible. 

Recently, the City celebrated Holman’s 100th birthday, declaring Dec. 26, 2025, as Alwin Benjamin Holman Day. 

#BlackHistoryMonth #SDFD #SanDiego #firefighter

title: Food Assistance During the Federal Government Shutdown
description:
If you receive CalFresh benefits, you have likely heard about the current federal government shutdown and its impact to your CalFresh benefits.    Here’s what you need to know:

The shutdown means that the federal government will not be authorizing CalFresh benefits for the month of November 2025. Once the shutdown ends, benefits will be issued to those who were eligible in the month of November. 

If your CalFresh SAR 7 or annual renewal is due during the shutdown, you MUST complete them on time to remain eligible so that you may continue to receive your benefits once the shutdown ends. 

We encourage you to visit your local food pantry and to connect with your local mutual aid organizations for assistance during this difficult time. 

For a list of locations, please visit LAFoodBank.org or contact 211 by dialing 2-1-1 or visiting www.211.org.

title: San Pedro Waterfront Gives Locals First Look at Massive West Harbor
description:
Soccer fans and local families got an exciting sneak peek at San Pedro’s new West Harbor project ahead of its official opening this fall. The redeveloped Port of Los Angeles Waterfront recently hosted the official World Cup LA Fan Zone, bringing neighbors together for live match broadcasts, local bites, and stunning ocean views.

Visitors enjoyed early tastes from upcoming dining spots like LoZio Pizza and The Baked Bear. The lively event transformed the former Ports O’ Call site into a safe, upbeat gathering space for all Angelenos.
Once completed, the new waterfront attraction will feature a mile-long promenade, harbor cruises, children's play areas, and a massive ferris wheel. Local residents say sharing these energetic moments with friends and family proves just how deeply sports and community spaces can unite people.

title: Regular City Council - 08/10/99
Update to Nonprofit Security Grants as Legislators in Sacramento Consider State Budget
description: SAN DIEGO, CA – San Diego City Councilmembers Marni von Wilpert, Chair of the Public Safety Committee, and Raul Campillo, Vice Chair of the Public Safety Committee, will hold a press briefing to give an update on Governor Gavin Newsom’s inclusion of $40 million in his revised state budget to support security enhancements for nonprofit organizations that have historically been targets of hate-motivated violence and attacks.  The update comes as the California legislature votes on Governor Newsom’s budget, and after the tragic shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego. Councilmembers von Wilpert and Campillo will discuss their urging of the California State Legislature to pass the $40 million Security Grant Program. This funding is what Councilmembers von Wilpert and Campillo advocated for earlier this year following the rise in hate-motivated violence targeting communities and religious institutions across California and the nation.

REVISED SPECIAL - Housing Committee - SAP - 9/08/26
How the Homeless Housing Recovery Program Is Changing Lives in Los Angeles
description:
What does it take to help someone break the cycle of homelessness? The Homeless Housing Recovery Program (HHRP) addresses the needs of people experiencing homelessness, mental illness, and substance use disorders in the West San Fernando Valley by helping remove barriers to long-term stability.

HHRP is a collaborative partnership between Council District 3, Providence Hospital, and the Tarzana Treatment Center. Patient navigators in hospital emergency rooms identify individuals at critical moments, such as after an overdose or fall, and refer them to the program instead of discharging them back to the streets.

Participants receive ongoing support throughout their recovery, including case management, transportation to medical appointments, and assistance navigating essential services. Many also receive rent-free housing, allowing them to focus on recovery, employment, and saving for their next step.

Over the past five years, HHRP has helped 120 people transition into permanent, non-subsidized housing, including moving into their own apartments or homes, paying their own rent, or reunifying with family both within and outside California.

Olinda Tiny Homes Village: One of L.A.’s Largest Opens
description:
One of the largest tiny home communities in the City of Los Angeles is opening its doors—providing 208 beds and a new path forward for unhoused Angelenos.

The Olinda Tiny Homes Village, located in Sun Valley, offers more than a safe place to stay. It connects residents with the security, resources, and personalized support they need to move toward stability and permanent housing.

Each residential unit is ADA accessible and includes a stowaway bunk bed, electrical outlets, heating and air conditioning, interior lighting, shelving, and storage. Residents also receive warm meals, street-outreach support, life-skills assistance, and access to dedicated case managers.

From obtaining a birth certificate or state identification to finding employment and preparing for permanent housing, every service is designed to help residents move forward. At Olinda Tiny Homes Village, stepping through the gates marks the beginning of a new chapter—and a reminder that no one has to face that journey alone.

title: Park to Park 2026: Open Streets Joins Two Parks Along Wilshire
description:
Metro helps fund open streets events across Los Angeles County, including Park to Park 2026, which transformed Wilshire Boulevard into a people-first public space. Over two days, the event connected MacArthur Park and Lafayette Park, creating miles of car-free streets for walking, biking, rolling, and enjoying the neighborhood.

With traffic temporarily rerouted, families, friends, and neighbors were able to explore Wilshire Boulevard in a new way—free from cars. Community members gathered to socialize, enjoy activities, and experience a clean, safe, and welcoming public space.

Beyond operating buses and trains, Metro invests in projects that expand transportation options and strengthen partnerships with local communities. Through funding for open streets events, construction, and shuttle services, Metro helps create more connected, accessible, and vibrant neighborhoods across Los Angeles.

On September 11, 2001, members of the Los Angeles Fire Department deployed to New York to help with search and rescue efforts at Ground Zero. Twenty-five years later, LAFD firefighters, city leaders and community members gathered at the Frank Hotchkin Memorial Training Center in Los Angeles to remember the lives lost and honor the first responders who answered the call.

This commemoration reflects on their courage, the bonds formed in a time of crisis, and the commitment to serve that continues.

Today, LAFD crews answer thousands of emergency calls daily, bringing that same passion and dedication to local neighborhoods. Community leaders emphasized that sticking together remains essential when facing modern challenges. Ultimately, honoring this milestone ensures future generations never forget what true bravery looks like when neighbors step up to protect one another.

title: Honoring Fallen Caltrans Crew Members in Los Angeles
description:
A sea of orange filled the area recently as Caltrans District 7 workers gathered for their annual memorial. The moving event honored 32 crew members who tragically lost their lives while keeping Los Angeles highways safe.

In a district where motorists travel 99 million miles every day, road crews face constant danger. These dedicated workers repair potholes, fences, and guardrails to ensure the traveling public stays safe. However, they face extreme risks from fast traffic, hazardous conditions, and distracted drivers.

A text message can wait, but a life can't. When drivers choose to put down their phones and focus on the road, they play a vital role in protecting the essential workers who keep California moving.

title: LA Is for Everyone: LA Kicks Off 5th Annual Week of Inclusion & Unity
description:
Los Angeles recently marked the fifth annual LA Is for Everyone Week, a citywide effort led by the Los Angeles Civil Rights Department to promote belonging, inclusion, solidarity, and civic participation.

Created in response to rising hate and discrimination, LA Is for Everyone has grown into more than a slogan. It reflects the City’s commitment to making sure every Angeleno feels seen, supported, and included.

During the event, City leaders highlighted programs such as REPAIR, community partnerships, and public education efforts like Know Your Rights outreach, all aimed at connecting residents with resources and creating more opportunities for communities to help shape local policies and priorities.

The message remained simple: Hate has no home here. LA is for everyone.

Learn more about the Los Angeles Civil Rights Department and its work to build a more inclusive Los Angeles.

https://civilandhumanrights.lacity.gov/

title: EMS Corps Ready to Serve and Care for Their Community
description:
Sixteen young men and women just graduated from the County’s first Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Corps, a 5-month-long, rigorous and nationally recognized Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) job training program. CAL FIRE/San Diego County Fire recruited Transitional Age Youth between the ages of 18 to 26 who have historically faced barriers to employment in the EMS field. The students received EMT training and wrap around supportive services to help them succeed, such as stipends, tutoring, mentoring, and job preparedness skills.

title: County Support Helps Kinship Caregivers Provide Stable Homes
description:
September is National Kinship Care Month, a time to  honor grandparents, aunts, uncles, adult siblings, godparents, stepparents and close family friends who step up to raise children when their parents can’t. In San Diego County, about half of all children in out-of-home care live with kinship caregivers.
 
Kin placements are preferred because they keep children connected to their families, traditions, and culture. But kinship care often begins suddenly, and relatives may not  have the resources to care for a child—especially one with medical or developmental needs.
 
County Child & Family Well Being t provides support and resources that help kinship caregivers create stable, safe homes where children can thrive.
 
For one local grandparent, that support made all the difference. With help from the County, she gained the tools she needed to provide the best possible care for  her granddaughter.

New sensory-friendly features include softer lighting, reduced noise, accessible seating, and designated hours for patrons who benefit from a calmer environment. A sensory forecast helps families plan their visits, while portable lights and sensory kits are available for checkout.

The Wilshire Branch Library is the eighth Los Angeles Public Library location to receive these accessibility improvements. More than 40 LAPL branches also offer sensory kits with tools designed to help patrons feel comfortable, supported, and free to be themselves.

From LEGO activities to community events, the library continues to provide a space where young Angelenos can learn, create, and connect.

Plan your visit: https://www.lapl.org/branches/wilshire

title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspection (SBC) August 6, 2026 Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission meeting of August 6, 2026, reviewed urgent issues across LA County jails, including rising in-custody deaths, poor sanitation, and gaps in medical and mental health care. Two recent deaths bring this year’s total to 24.

Commissioners highlighted ongoing concerns with unsafe conditions, retaliation fears around grievances, and staffing shortages that leave incarcerated individuals waiting for essential services. Inspectors also reported deputies disengaged from duties, inconsistent oversight, and failures to provide special diets and basic hygiene.

The Commission welcomed Yana Grammer, underscoring a continued focus on accountability, transparency, and expanding mental health treatment options beyond jail facilities.

title: Get It Done App: Now More Accessible Than Ever!
description:
We’re working to make sure tools like our Get It Done app are accessible to everyone.  

Thank you to the National Federation of the Blind of California San Diego Chapter for partnering with the City’s Performance & Analytics Department (PandA) and ADA Compliance and Accessibility teams to test the newest version of the Get It Done app. Participants worked through real-world reporting scenarios, helping identify accessibility challenges and providing valuable feedback to improve the experience for all users. 

The updated Get It Done app includes a streamlined reporting process, enhanced accessibility features and better compatibility with screen readers, making it easier than ever to report non-emergency issues like potholes, graffiti and more. 

The thoughtful feedback from this group of testers will help make the Get It Done app more accessible and improve the experience for everyone who uses it. 

Download or update the Get It Done app today and help keep San Diego safe, clean and connected: sandiego.gov/get-it-done.

#GetItDone #Accessibility #SanDiego

description:
Not a city of San Diego resident? Our staff help explain what visitors and those living outside of the city of San Diego need to know about free and paid parking at Balboa Park. 

Generally, you’ll need to use the parking kiosks located around the park to purchase parking, unless you’re looking for long-term monthly or annual passes. Those are available at sandiego.thepermitportal.com.  

Follow the signs posted in each parking lot to determine the daily and hourly rates.  

You CAN still park for free in Balboa Park. The Lower Inspiration Point lot is free for up to three hours and there’s a free tram available to transport you to the center of Balboa Park.

description:
SAN DIEGO – Chelsea Investment Corporation, County Supervisor Monica Montgomery-Steppe, San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria, and Councilmember Dr. Jennifer Campbell gathered to celebrate the grand opening of Terrasini, a 95-unit affordable housing development for individuals aged 62+.
Older adults are the fastest-growing population experiencing homelessness in San Diego, often due to job loss or serious illness. They struggle to afford rent on monthly incomes as low as $1,200 and often have to choose between food and medicine. Terrasini will change the quality of life for 95 San Diego seniors who struggle to find a safe and affordable place to call home.

title: Meet Your Parks: Four Gee County Park
description:
Four Gee County Park
16964 Four Gee Road, San Diego, CA 92127
Park: (858) 673-3990 
Hours: Sunrise – sunset, daily

Four Gee County Park opened in Spring 2024. This neighborhood park in San Diego's 4S Ranch community measures over 1 acre and features a variety of amenities including a large shade-covered playground, a lawn, and built-in chess and ping-ping tables, and cornhole boards.

Dog owners enjoy the fenced, off-leash dog areas and themed agility equipment, along with a drinking fountain that accommodates both dogs and their owners.

Walkers and hikers can stroll the perimeter path and take a seat on benches and picnic tables.

On-site plants and trees are drought-tolerant and watered by smart irrigation systems to support regional sustainability measures. Many of them are also native to the area, encouraging the health and longevity of local wildlife. 

The park was built with ADA parking, bike parking, restrooms, a water refilling station, a grill, and an educational kiosk to publicize safety information and upcoming activities. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Momentum in motion 💧

Work is progressing across Pure Water San Diego as crews complete key sections throughout the project! Recent milestones include pipeline connections, pump station improvements, and the start of final road resurfacing around Bay Park.

By capturing and purifying wastewater that would otherwise be discharged, Pure Water San Diego is helping reduce ocean discharges while safely conveying and treating recycled water. Each step moves us closer to a more sustainable, locally controlled water supply for San Diego, reducing dependence on imported water and strengthening reliability for our communities.

Santa Monica honored the legacy of Silas White with street renaming
description:
Santa Monica honored the legacy of Silas White with the renaming of a portion of Vicente Terrace to Silas White Street.

White was a prominent Black entrepreneur in Santa Monica in the 1950’s who envisioned creating the Ebony Beach Club, a space where Black families could gather and enjoy the beach.

The ceremony marked an important step in the city’s ongoing restorative justice work, acknowledging our history and honoring those who helped shape our community.

The renaming follows Santa Monica City Council’s settlement agreement with the White family and the establishment of Oct. 12 as Silas White Day in Santa Monica.

title: San Carlos Affordable Housing Project Breaks Ground on 44 New Homes
description: San Diego - Forty-four individuals and families, including those with intellectual or developmental disabilities, will soon have a new place to call home in San Carlos. On Tuesday, June 16, Mayor Todd Gloria and City staff joined Community HousingWorks and other local leaders to celebrate the groundbreaking of the Navajo Family Apartments located at 7005 Navajo Road. The one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments will be affordable to households making 30% to 70% of the area median income. Eight of the homes will be reserved for community members with intellectual or developmental disabilities and come with project-based vouchers from the San Diego Housing Commission. Project-based vouchers allow rental assistance to be attached to a specific unit and/or project instead of to an eligible assisted family.

description:
El Niño may bring significant weather impacts to our communities this fall and winter, including the possibility of heavy rainfall. Here's how you can protect yourself and your loved ones: 

✓ Have a portable emergency go kit. Make sure valuables, documents and medications are readily available and in waterproof containers.

✓ Have an evacuation plan. Identify a location to meet up with loved ones and ways to communicate. 

✓ Sign up for emergency alerts.

✓ Make sure your car is in good condition, check windshield wipers and tires.

✓ Have flashlights handy.

Learn more: sandiego.gov/elnino

#StayReadySanDiego #ElNiño #NationalPreparednessMonth

description:
The city of Santa Monica is making progress on the East Pico safety Project, improving one of the city’s busiest corridors along East Pico Boulevard from 26th St. to Centinela Ave.

The project is scheduled to wrap up this week before Thanksgiving. Crews are adding finishing touches, reconstructing pavement, upgrading  bus pads and painting new striping and installing signage and markings, to give Pico a smoother, safer and more vibrant look.

This work aligns with the city’s Realignment Plan and its ongoing commitment to safe neighborhoods and clean streets across Santa Monica.

title: Aircraft Media Day Press Briefing 9/3/26
description:
Los Angeles County is teaming up with Canadian partners once again to tackle peak wildfire season. Two iconic "Super Scooper" aircraft have officially returned to Van Nuys Airport, marking 33 years of vital international teamwork.

These massive planes can scoop 1,600 gallons of water in seconds, providing crucial rapid response for local crews. Fire officials warned that heavy spring rains grew extra vegetation, which summer heat has now dried into dangerous wildfire fuel.

"Equipment alone cannot keep our community safe," said Supervisor Kathryn Barger, urging residents to prepare. Officials ask all homeowners to clear dry brush around properties and create emergency evacuation plans before high winds hit.

More than 25 Canadian pilots and technicians will remain stationed in Southern California alongside LA County firefighters. Together, these brave teams stand ready 24/7 to safeguard homes and save lives.

Is Your Emergency Kit Ready? Essential Tips for Every Home
description:
Disasters can strike Los Angeles—or any community—at a moment’s notice, from sudden earthquakes to severe weather. That’s why City leaders are urging all Angelenos to take action during National Preparedness Month this September.

Because Los Angeles covers such a vast area, first responders may not be able to reach every neighborhood immediately during a crisis. In those critical early hours, neighbors often serve as one another’s first lifeline. Staying connected and helping those nearby can make entire communities safer.

Preparing today helps ensure your household is ready for whatever comes tomorrow. Residents and business owners should review their emergency plans, practice evacuation routes, and check disaster kits for essential supplies.

Small steps now can make a significant difference later. Visit https://ready.lacity.gov/ for disaster preparedness guides, emergency checklists, and community resources to help protect you and your loved ones.

#LACityResidents #ReadyLA

title: Building Sand Berms Ahead of Storm Season
description:
With a strong El Niño in the forecast this fall and winter, the City's beach mechanized team is installing sand berms on City beaches and the Mission Bay shoreline. 

Crews use large equipment to move and shape sand into berms, which are intended to protect against flooding caused by high tides and surf. The berms are installed annually ahead of the winter storm season, and with strong El Niño conditions predicted this year, emergency officials are urging extra precautions.

While flooding in coastal areas can occur during winter storms, particularly when combined with high tides, anticipated El Niño conditions could increase that risk and affect locations that do not typically experience flooding.

Berm installation is anticipated to take several weeks, starting on the bay and then moving along the beach shoreline to be completed by early November: insidesandiego.org/city-prepares-beaches-and-bay-shoreline-winter-storms

#CityOfSanDiego #ENSO #ElNino #Beach

title: Regular City Council - 07/16/99
Regular City Council - 02/04/98
The Women Who Fought to Break Into LAPD
description:
They were told they didn’t belong — but they showed up anyway and demanded the chance to prove they did. 

From the very beginning, women in the Los Angeles Police Department faced resistance at every level, with one early voice recalling, “I don’t want anybody to give me something I haven’t earned — just the opportunity to earn it.” This is the story of how determination and grit cracked open doors that were never meant to open.

Historians trace these barriers back to the department’s earliest days, when societal norms confined women to the home and policing was considered strictly male work. As Los Angeles grew, so did the need for change — especially in areas like juvenile services — yet opportunities for women remained limited or nonexistent. Even as they entered the force, they were met with outdated beliefs and blatant discrimination, including claims that women couldn’t lead. Still, these officers pushed forward, determined to prove they could do the job just as well, if not better.

Through resilience and relentless effort, they transformed the department from within. Women rose through the ranks to become lieutenants, captains, pilots, detectives, and beyond — fulfilling what once seemed impossible, including the long-held vision of one day seeing a female chief. As one historian noted, real progress requires confronting the painful parts of history — and these women did exactly that. Their legacy isn’t just about breaking barriers; it’s about redefining what leadership, strength, and service look like in one of the most demanding professions in the world.

title: Cleaning Up City of San Diego Encampments
description:
Over the last three Fridays, City crews and contractors have connected at least 21 people experiencing homelessness to sheltering options in a three-block area of downtown. 

This targeted operation starts with a compassionate approach: offering available programs and services before crews go in to remove trash and sanitize the area.

This work near K and 17th street happens three days a week, but the City is responding to concerns from nearby businesses and stepping up sheltering and trash-removal efforts. 

Please submit Get It Done reports for unsafe encampments located on City property. Every report is followed up on. While people may return to areas once they are cleaned, crews will be back out again soon to offer sheltering options and sanitize the area. 

#SanDiego

title: Creating Freedom Quilt Mosaics for Black History Month
description:
In one of many events celebrating Black History Month this February, San Diego Public Library has held Freedom Quilt Workshops across San Diego — most recently at the City Heights/Weingart Library. 

Presented by ToshWerks, participants craft their own miniature quilts inspired by tales of resilience, creativity and courage during the time of the Underground Railroad.

description: Videos provided to you by the City of Santa Monica.
transcript_text: Okay, well, I'm going to call this meeting to order at 7:13 on Monday, October 12th. Um, welcome everybody. Uh, our well, let's do our, uh, roll call. So, we're all the way down to item four, consent calendar, and we are at approval of minutes from the September 21st regular meeting. Would anyone like to move approval of the minutes? >> I move to approve. >> Second. >> Move. >> [laughter] >> It was just off Mike at first. >> For the record, Alex Tower moved to approve and David Pettit approved. Thank you. [laughter] >> Great. Is there any discussion? No? And no changes to any of the minutes? Okay, so all in favor? >> I. >> I. That passes unanimously. And now we are on to the fun part. Continued items 5A overview of the 2025 greenhouse gas emissions inventory with Elias. Take it away. >> Ooh, the fun part. Hey everybody, Elias Pattison. You know, I'm a sustainability analyst in the office of sustainability working under Ariana and Shannon. Is the mic okay? Clovis? I think this was the right Yeah. Facing you. I'll just [clears throat and snorts] stick with this one. Can do. All right. So, I'm here to talk about the city's most recently completed community greenhouse gas or GHG emissions inventory that our team just wrapped up a couple weeks ago and I worked on this report alongside members of my team including our Civic Spark fellow who's here today, Fiona Dubey. Some of you may have met her. She's presented to the commission before, but she was a huge help in completing this inventory. So, really appreciate her support. For a little bit of background, you're probably all aware but the city passed or adopted its climate action and adaptation plan or the cap back in 2019. And the CAP set several greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets. So, the first interim target was an 80% reduction of GHG emissions below 1990 levels by 2030. So, 1990 is our baseline. That's the first year that the city uh conducted a GHG emissions inventory. And then we have an ultimate goal of carbon neutrality by 2050 or sooner. So, that's where we're headed. Today I'll talk about where we're at in that journey and what we got to do to to close the gap. Um and then our team likes to do these GHG emissions inventories about every 2 years just cuz it's, you know, a lot of work and really we're trying to focus more on the actions that'll help us get to the emissions reductions as opposed to doing constant check-ins. But I think every 2 years is a good cadence. Uh and then the city shares not only with the public and council members of the community, but uh with the Carbon Disclosure Project the results of our community greenhouse gas emissions inventory. So, we just submitted that in mid-September. We're waiting back on a score, but we expect to do pretty well based on uh how the results of this report shaped up and how we've done in previous years. Just for a little bit more context, um the Climate Action Adaptation Plan or the CAP, as you can imagine, is split into two main parts. So, there's the climate action piece, which is about reducing emissions and preventing, you know, the worst of uh climate change by limiting our impact on it. And then the second half is climate adaptation, which we won't talk too much about today, but it is um a big of our team's work. But on the climate action side, the plan is split into kind of three main buckets. So, zero net carbon buildings, zero waste, and then sustainable mobility. Um and then climate action, there's a couple different overarching goals there that, you know, are also becoming more important in Santa Monica as we're starting to feel the effects of climate change right in our backyard. But we're talking mostly about climate action today since that's what uh is more relevant to the GHG inventory. In terms of methodology, we follow the global protocol for community scale GHG inventories or the GPC framework. And that means that we do a sector-based inventory, which basically measures emissions produced within the geographic boundary of Santa Monica across a number of different sectors. So, we're looking at energy in the residential sector, the commercial and the industrial sector. We're looking at vehicle transportation, so all the vehicles that are traveling within Santa Monica or starting trips outside of Santa Monica and ending in Santa Monica and vice versa. And then since we have an airport, we're also tracking aviation emissions and then emissions from waste sent to landfills from, you know, facilities in Santa Monica as well as water and wastewater emissions. And then something called process and fugitive emissions, which is basically emissions that occur from, you know, transporting gas into facilities and buildings. There's some that essentially escape and need to be counted. So, we claim those emissions as well. And to do the inventory, we use a tool called ICLEI ClearPath. And ClearPath just did a big revamp. This is our first time doing the inventory in their 2.0 version. So, there's a couple different methodology shifts that I'll try to flag for you all, but it means that it was a different process this year than in in previous years. >> [clears throat] >> And then we report emissions in metric tons of CO2 equivalent. So, not every emission is carbon dioxide, but to kind of standardize methane emissions and nitrous oxide emissions and CO2 emissions, we report one CO2 equivalent number. So, that's that's the metric that you're going to see the emissions that we're talking about in. And so, this is a uh kind of overarching trajectory of where we have come from in terms of our emissions journey. Again, we started measuring in 1990, so that's our baseline year. We were all the way up near 1.4 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent that year, and there's been roughly a steady decline since then. • Գործունեության դադարեցումը նշանակում է, որ դաշնային կառավարությունը չի հաստատելու CalFresh նպաստները 2025 թվականի նոյեմբեր ամսվա համար։
• Երբ գործունեության դադարը ավարտվի, նպաստները կտրամադրվեն այն անձանց, ովքեր իրավասու էին 2025 թվականի նոյեմբեր ամսին։

Extreme high tides are expected along San Diego's coast starting Saturday, July 11, through July 15, and some low-lying coastal areas may see temporary flooding. 

During the high tides, the City's Stormwater Department increases warning signs and deploys additional staff in the Midway neighborhood and other tide‑impacted areas to help keep motorists safe. Teams will also be monitoring low-lying areas in Mission Beach and are prepared to respond if flooding occurs. 

If you live or park in flood‑prone areas, now is a good time to plan ahead: 
• Use sandbags where appropriate. 
• Avoid parking vehicles in areas known to flood. 
• Stay alert for posted signage and changing conditions. 

The City offers free unfilled sandbags for San Diego residents at select recreation centers. Find locations and more preparedness tips on the City's Storm Preparedness page at sandiego.gov/storm-preparedness.

title: The Wild West Isn't What You Think! Inside LA's Autry Museum
description:
What if everything you thought you knew about the Wild West was only part of the story?

Hollywood often portrays cowboys as lone white heroes, but history tells a much richer and more diverse story. Nestled in Griffith Park, the Autry Museum of the American West challenges these familiar myths, bringing the history, art, and cultures of the American West to life.

Founded in 1988 by legendary singing cowboy Gene Autry and his wife, Jackie, the museum explores the often-overlooked contributions of Black cowboys, women, Native Americans, and immigrants who helped shape the West. In fact, historians estimate that roughly one in four cowboys was Black.

Through fascinating artifacts, immersive exhibitions, Western art, and extensive collections of Native American cultural objects, the Autry explores the complex history of the American West, from Indigenous traditions and westward expansion to the conflicts and cultural exchanges that shaped the region.

Discover why the American West is so much more than cowboys, horses, and Hollywood legends—and why this Los Angeles cultural landmark deserves a spot on your must-visit list.

Current and Upcoming Exhibits include: 
🌵Promised Lands: California's Unratified Treaties and Native Resilience, September 26, 2026–July 30, 2028

🌵Life, Liberty, and Los Angeles
May 30, 2026 - January 31, 2027

🌵Creative Continuities: Family, Pride, and Community in Native Art
November 15, 2025 – June 27, 2027

📍 Autry Museum of the American West
Griffith Park, Los Angeles
Learn more: https://theautry.org/

title: New E-Bike Regulations to Take Effect in San Diego
description:
The City of San Diego is launching a public education and outreach campaign on e-bike safety ahead of new regulations for kids. City Councilmember Raul Campillo was joined by the San Diego Police Department (SDPD), the San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) Police Department, and local Girl Scout Troop 4343 outside Montgomery Middle School to announce the outreach effort.

Recently approved e-bike regulations impose a minimum age of 12 years for Class One and Two e-bikes, essentially making a pedal bike the only bike approved for kids under 12. Class Three e-bikes already require individuals to be 16 years or older to operate under state law.

Regular City Council - 6/9/26
Inside Los Angeles' Newest Tiny Home Community
description:
Take a look inside one of Los Angeles' newest Tiny Home communities.

A new Tiny Home community has opened in Council District 2, providing 100 beds for individuals experiencing homelessness. Each 64-square-foot home accommodates two residents and includes electricity, four windows, a bed, and a locking front door for added security. 

The site also features laundry facilities, a communal dining area, and supportive services designed to help residents transition from the streets to permanent housing. Hear from City leaders, service providers, and residents about how these Tiny Home communities are creating stability, restoring dignity, and offering hope to Angelenos in need.

title: Women Who Need CPR Are Less Likely To Get It
description:
It's a troubling statistic. Women are 14% less likely to receive CPR in public emergencies. (39% of women get CPR compared to 45% for men). 

Often, people fear touching a stranger's chest and hurting them while administering CPR. Good Samaritan laws protect people who step in to give reasonable emergency help. Everyone deserves help in an emergency. Learning CPR and acting fast can save a life!

More info: sandiego.gov/sdprojectheartbeat/training

#CPR #CityOfSanDiego

title: "Am I Sorting My Bins Right?"
description:
Today is America Recycles Day! Let’s keep our planet clean by sorting our waste the right way: 

Green Bin: 
✅ Kitchen food scraps and yard trimmings go in the green bin (in brown paper bags if you like). Reminder: Plastic and compostable plastic bags go in the trash bin. 
🚫No hoses, dog toys or pet waste. 

Blue Bin: 
✅Place clean and dry recyclables loosely in the bin. Got clothes? Try donating instead of tossing them! 
🚫 No plastic bags. 

Gray/Black Bin: 
✅Pet waste, plastic and compostable plastic bags and takeout containers. 
🚫 No electronic-waste or lithium-ion batteries. They can cause trash truck fires! Visit sandiego.gov/hazwaste to learn how to dispose of them safely. 

Thanks, San Diego, for your part in helping our environment! 🌎💚 

Wondering what goes where? We have guides available: sandiego.gov/environmental-services/recycling/residential/curbside

The initiative includes 27 Champion Grants for 2027 supporting youth-serving organizations and programs, including flag football, coaching, equipment, transportation, and access to places to play.

Super Bowl LXI may last just one day, but organizers are working to make its community impact last well beyond the final whistle.

title: Spring-Alameda Safety & Mobility Project 9/10/26
description:
Los Angeles city leaders officially broke ground on the Spring Alameda Safety and Mobility Project. This major street overhaul transforms a 1.2-mile stretch connecting Chinatown, Union Station, and the LA State Historic Park into a safer, more accessible space for everyone.

Between 2013 and 2022, vehicles struck 46 pedestrians and cyclists along this high-risk corridor. To prevent future traffic violence, city crews are adding protected bike lanes, rebuilt curb ramps, high-visibility crosswalks, and two new pedestrian signals.

More than 2,000 community members helped design the new features. These additions will make walking and biking safer for families, local seniors, and transit riders accessing parks and neighboring businesses.

Work is already underway, with full completion expected by early next summer. These infrastructure upgrades will serve local neighborhoods for generations, long after the 2028 Olympic Games conclude.

title: LA Currents: LA City Clerk Patrice Lattimore
description:
What does the Los Angeles City Clerk do, and why does the office play such an important role in local government?

In this episode of LA Currents, host Anita Bennett sits down with Los Angeles City Clerk Patrice Lattimore, the first Black woman to hold the position, to explore how her office supports elections, preserves nearly 200 years of City history, and promotes transparency and civic engagement.

With more than 26 years of City service, Lattimore shares how the City Clerk's Office helps Angelenos stay informed through voter education, election outreach, and access to City Council meetings and public records.

The conversation also explores preparations for the 2027 Neighborhood Council elections, including the return of in-person voting alongside vote-by-mail, as well as efforts to expand language access, improve accessibility, and digitize historical records dating back to the 1800s.

From preserving historic treasures like the Griffith Park deed and the 1984 Olympic flag to mentoring the next generation of public servants, Lattimore reflects on her leadership, commitment to public service, and vision for a more accessible and inclusive City government.

Discover how the Los Angeles City Clerk's Office works behind the scenes to keep residents informed, engaged, and connected to their local government.

Learn more: https://clerk.lacity.gov/

#LACityGovernment #LACityClerk

title: Super Scoopers Take Flight to Defend Southern California
description:
Two Canadair CL-415 Super Scoopers have returned to Van Nuys Airport to help protect Southern California communities during wildfire season. The aircraft support Los Angeles County and may assist neighboring counties through California’s regional mutual-aid system.

For the 33rd consecutive year, the Government of Québec has provided the aircraft, along with experienced pilots and mechanics. The planes give local firefighters a powerful tool from the air, scooping water and delivering it quickly to wildfires.

However, fire officials remind residents that firefighting equipment alone cannot protect every home. Community preparedness and preventive action remain essential to keeping neighborhoods safe.

This longstanding international partnership demonstrates how governments and emergency-response agencies can work together to protect communities during wildfire season.

title: Silas White Renaming Street
description:
Santa Monica honored the legacy of Silas White with the renaming of a portion of Vicente Terrace to Silas White Street.

White was a prominent Black entrepreneur in Santa Monica in the 1950’s who envisioned creating the Ebony Beach Club, a space where Black families could gather and enjoy the beach.

The ceremony marked an important step in the city’s ongoing restorative justice work, acknowledging our history and honoring those who helped shape our community.

The renaming follows Santa Monica City Council’s settlement agreement with the White family and the establishment of Oct. 12 as Silas White Day in Santa Monica.

South LA Youth Turn Tragedy Into Action With AB 2318
description:
Community members, youth activists, and emergency medical professionals gathered outside Santee High School in South Los Angeles to advocate for fair treatment and timely medical care for people injured during law enforcement actions.

Their efforts helped inspire California Assembly Bill 2318, which would require law enforcement to provide prompt medical aid once a scene is secure. If care is delayed or withheld, officers would be required to submit written documentation explaining why.

Developed with young organizers from Voters of Tomorrow, the legislation grew out of concerns that injured community members were not receiving timely medical attention. By helping write the bill and bringing their advocacy to the state level, these young leaders are turning community concerns into meaningful policy reform.

To address the Board, you are encouraged to register by visiting www.publiccomment.lacounty.gov; registration opens at 9:00 a.m. the day of the meeting:

Press * to access the menu and follow the prompts
- 1 - Listen only
- 3 - Speak on the active item
- 0 - Request to register for multiple items

If selected, you will receive a text message reminder when your item is up for discussion on the agenda.

New trees are sprouting up across San Diego!
description:
New trees are sprouting up across San Diego! In fact, the City planted more than 5,000 trees in 2025, and more than 14,000 since 2020. 🌳

Trees provide shade and help cool our neighborhoods, clean the air, support wildlife and reduce climate pollution. Many of these new trees were planted through the grant-funded Ready, Set, Grow San Diego initiative, which focused planting efforts in City Heights, Bay Terraces, Linda Vista, Oak Park, Otay Mesa-Nestor, Paradise Hills and Encanto. 

While the planting phase of this initiative is now complete, the work continues with protecting existing trees and redesigning sidewalks to support long-term tree health. 

#SDClimateWeek #UrbanForestry #ClimateAction

Discover the FREE Art Gallery Inside Los Angeles City Hall
description:
Discover a hidden art gallery inside Los Angeles City Hall! The Henry P. Rio Bridge Gallery, known as the “People’s Gallery,” is a rotating exhibition space that celebrates the diverse cultures, histories, and communities that shape Los Angeles.

Managed by the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs, the gallery features rotating exhibitions throughout the year, highlighting Latino, African American, Native American, LGBTQIA+, and other cultural perspectives through art.

The exhibition featured in the video is "Corazón de Los Ángeles: The Art of Chicano Politics & Community Healing," presented by AltaMed Health Services. The exhibition showcases historic and contemporary artwork that honors cultural roots, community identity, and artistic expression.

Free and open to the public during City Hall’s public access hours, the Henry P. Rio Bridge Gallery invites Angelenos to explore its ever-changing exhibitions and discover the art and stories that connect the people of Los Angeles.

title: Transportation Committee - 12/10/25
Our SMPD Family: An Inspiring Talk with Sgt. Elaina Hassan & K9 Jack (Thanksgiving Special)
description:
​👮‍♀️ A Look Inside the Badge: Sgt. Elaina Hassan & K9 Jack's Story (Thanksgiving Special)

​This Thanksgiving week, we're taking a moment to celebrate the family that supports our Santa Monica Police Department (SMPD) and introducing you to one of our finest: Sergeant Elaina Hassan.

​In this exclusive interview, Sgt. Hassan opens up about her journey: from her college days and early career in Arizona to finding her true professional home here at the SMPD. She shares what inspired her to serve and the powerful role her family plays in her demanding career.

​🌟 What You'll See in This Video:
​The Journey to SMPD: Hear about her well-rounded background, including her education in Arizona, and why she chose to join the Santa Monica Police Department.

title: 연방 정부 셧다운(임시 업무 정지)에 대해 DPSS에서 드리는 중요한 메시지입니다.
description:
혜택을 받고 있는 경우, 현재 연방 정부 셧다운(임시 업무 정지)와 그것이 CalFresh에 미치는 영향에 대해 들어보셨을 것입니다. 

알아두셔야 할 사항은 다음과 같습니다:
• 셧다운(임시 업무 정지)는 연방 정부가 2025년 11월 한 달 동안 CalFresh 혜택을 승인하지 않는다는 것을 의미합니다. 
• 셧다운(임시 업무 정지)이 끝나면, 11월에 자격이 있었던 사람들에게 혜택이 지급됩니다.  
• 셧다운(임시 업무 정지) 기간 동안 CalFresh SAR 7 또는 연례 갱신 마감일이 있는 경우, 셧다운(임시 업무 정지)가 종료된 후에도 혜택을 계속 받을 수 있도록 자격을 유지하려면 제 때에 갱신을 완료해야 합니다. 
이 어려운 시기에 도움을 받기 원하시면, 해당 지역 무료 식품 배급소를 방문하고 지역 상호 원조 단체와 연결하여 도움을 받는 것이 좋습니다. 

위치 목록은, 웹사이트 LAFoodBank.org 를 방문하시거나, 2-1-1으로 전화 또는 웹사이트 www.211.org를 방문하여 211에 연락하십시오.

Inside Cabrillo Marine Aquarium’s New Jelly Lab
description:
Step inside L.A.’s hidden underwater world and explore the stunning new Jelly Tunnel at Cabrillo Marine Aquarium.

Visitors can explore a maze of habitats, from coastal exhibits to the brand-new Jelly Lab. This state-of-the-art space raises baby jellies for research and education, giving guests the chance to walk through a “jelly tunnel” for a close-up look at beautiful purple-striped and moon jellies.

For 90 years, Cabrillo Marine Aquarium has served as a gateway to the Pacific, connecting the community with the vibrant marine life found right off our shores. This local gem is more than an attraction. It is a center for education and conservation that brings people of all backgrounds together.

Behind the scenes, a high-tech pump house helps ensure every animal receives the highest quality care. Whether you are learning about whales or watching jellies pulse in the light, the aquarium offers a peaceful glimpse into Southern California’s diverse marine world.

Come celebrate nearly a century of ocean discovery and help protect the incredible animals that call our coast home.

Visit the aquarium: https://cma.recreation.parks.lacity.gov/

title: Connect homeless individuals to critical resources
description:
Outreach teams and community partners are contacting people in encampments along the San Diego River to help move people experiencing homelessness out of dangerous areas and into shelters, housing or other supportive programs. 

This work is especially important with forecasters predicting a strong El Niño storm that could bring heavy rain and flooding to the region starting in the fall. This area is prone to flooding and individuals have been rescued in the past during heavy rains. 

Teams from the County of San Diego, San Diego Fire-Rescue Department, PATH San Diego, Healthcare in Action, San Diego River Park Foundation and PAVE San Diego are working throughout the 17-mile stretch of river to help connect individuals to critical resources.

title: Office of Public Accountability: Your Questions, Answered
description:
Who protects Angelenos when decisions are made about water and power? Meet the Office of Public Accountability (OPA), the City of Los Angeles’ official Ratepayer Advocate.

Operating independently of the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP), OPA represents the interests of the 4 million Angelenos and nearly 250,000 businesses that depend on LADWP services. Established through a voter-approved amendment to the Los Angeles City Charter, the office promotes transparency and accountability while helping ensure LADWP delivers safe, reliable, affordable, and clean water and power.

OPA also supports the City’s goals for climate action, equity, and long-term sustainability—helping ensure that the needs of ratepayers remain at the center of important utility decisions.

Learn more or contact the Office of Public Accountability:

📍 Los Angeles City Hall
200 N. Spring Street, Suite 1736
Los Angeles, CA 90012
📞 (213) 978-0220

title: 這裡是來自DPSS 有關聯邦政府停擺的重要通知
description:
如果你有 CalFresh 福利，你可能已經聽到有關最近聯邦政府停擺以及對你的 CalFresh 福利的影響。
以下是你需要知道的事項：
• 政府停擺意味著聯邦政府將不會批准 2025 年 11 月份的 CalFresh 福利。
• 政府停擺結束後，福利將會發放給哪些在 11 月份符合資格的人。
• 如果你的 CalFresh SAR 7 或年度續期申請在政府停擺期間到期時，你必須按時完成續期申請才能保持資格，這樣你在政府停擺結束後仍能繼續領取福利。
在這個困難的時期，我們鼓勵你到你當地的食物銀行，並與你所在社區的互助團體聯繫以尋求援助。

要查看哪裡有食物銀行，請訪問  LAFoodBank.org ，或撥打 2-1-1 聯繫 211 服務專線，亦可瀏覽 www.211.org 查詢相關資訊。

title: What is cyanography?
description:
Hidden behind the trees in Tujunga is one of Los Angeles’ best-kept creative secrets—the McGroarty Arts Center! 

During its summer arts workshops, participants explored the mesmerizing world of cyanotype, one of the earliest forms of photography. Using a special chemical process, natural sunlight, and a little creativity, artists transformed everyday objects into striking blue-and-white prints. 

From trending crafts to timeless techniques, the McGroarty Arts Center makes arts education affordable and accessible while bringing people together through creativity and community.

Learn more about upcoming classes at McGroarty Arts Center https://www.mcgroartyartscenter.org/

title: A Little Break Goes A Long Way For Kona
description:
The Dog Day Out Program at County Animal Services’ Bonita shelter gives dogs more than a break from the kennel — it gives them a chance to decompress, explore, and show who they are beyond the shelter environment.

Follow along with Natasha, a dedicated volunteer, and Kona, a lovable German shepherd, as they head out for a day of fresh air, exercise, and enrichment.

Through Dog Day Out, dogs benefit from:
• Socialization and physical activity
• Mental stimulation and stress relief
• Real-world experiences that help showcase their personalities to potential adopters

Natasha volunteers twice a week and says even a short outing can make a meaningful difference for shelter dogs.

Learn more about the Dog Day Out Program and volunteer opportunities at https://www.sddac.com
Dog Day Out is offered exclusively through the Bonita shelter.

title: The Heartbeat of Watts: 41st Annual Day of the Drum Festival
description:
The 41st Annual Watts Towers Day of the Drum Festival brought rhythm, culture, and community together at the Watts Towers Arts Center campus.

Presented by the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs, the festival celebrates the powerful role drumming plays across cultures and generations. Featuring acoustic drumming and traditions from across the African diaspora, the event creates opportunities to learn about history, instruments, cultural traditions, and the shared connection created through music.

The festival also highlights the importance of preserving drum culture while expanding access to arts, music, museum, and educational experiences in the Watts community.

Visit the Watts Towers Arts Center campus to experience its rich cultural history, exhibitions, programs, and community arts offerings.

title: Los Angeles Started Right Here in 1781
description:
Step into 245 years of Los Angeles history—without spending a dime!

On September 4, Los Angeles commemorates the founding of the pueblo in 1781. From its Indigenous roots and early settlers to the many communities that continue to shape it, Los Angeles has a rich and complex history.

Explore that history with a FREE walking tour led by the docents of Las Angelitas del Pueblo. Tours of El Pueblo Historical Monument feature Olvera Street, Pico House, Avila Adobe, and other significant landmarks.
📅 Thursday through Saturday
🕙 Tours begin at 10 a.m., 11 a.m., and noon
💲 Free

Discover the people, places, and cultures that have contributed to the story of Los Angeles.

title: LA's First Speed Cameras: How They Work and What Drivers Need to Know
description:
Los Angeles is rolling out its first automated speed cameras to reduce dangerous speeding, prevent traffic fatalities, and make neighborhood streets safer for drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists.

Through the Los Angeles Department of Transportation's (LADOT) Speed Safety System pilot program, cameras will detect vehicles traveling at least 11 mph over the posted speed limit. Designed with privacy protections, the cameras capture license plate information needed for enforcement, not drivers' faces.

Beginning October 26, 2026, the first cameras will activate with a 60-day warning period before citations are issued.

Similar programs are already showing promising results. Oakland reported a 70% reduction in excessive speeding at camera locations, while San Francisco reported an 84% reduction.

Hear from City leaders, traffic safety advocates, and crash survivors about how automated speed enforcement could help prevent tragedies and make Los Angeles streets safer for everyone.

title: Changing a Light Bulb 1000' Above Los Angeles
description:
Radio tower technicians climb the massive tower beside the Hollywood Sign, where they replace a critical beacon light at the very top. Hundreds of feet above the ground, every step matters, and safety is always on their minds.

Behind the scenes, these towers power the radio network that police, firefighters, and emergency crews depend on every day. This system runs 24/7, helping teams stay connected when seconds count. The radios they use are a lifeline, and keeping them working is a matter of life and death.

Most people never think about what happens on these towers. But through wind, weather, and constant wear, crews climb, repair, and maintain the equipment that keeps the City of Los Angeles moving. It’s demanding, high-risk work that quietly keeps everyone safe.

title: The 818’s Young Artists Are Taking Center Stage
description:
Musicians and artists in the San Fernando Valley often travel “over the hill” for gigs, jam sessions, networking, and creative community—but the 818 has a vibrant arts scene of its own.

“818 Creates: Young Creatives Festival” celebrates the Valley’s talented artists and creates more opportunities for them to connect, collaborate, and showcase their work close to home. At Taxco Theatre, an ongoing immersive gallery features artwork from young artists and local community organizations, along with creative partners from across the San Fernando Valley—including Sun Valley.

With support from the City of Los Angeles, the festival is helping make the arts more accessible in a region that is not always recognized as an arts destination. Creative spaces allow people to explore their identities, experiences, and spirituality while building empathy and meaningful connections with others. 

Experience the creativity emerging throughout the San Fernando Valley—and discover what it might inspire you to create.

title: The Dangerous and Unpredictable Job of an LA Park Ranger
description:
Behind the badge of an LA City Park Ranger, there is no such thing as a typical day.

From confronting armed suspects and tracking repeat fire offenders to rescuing lost hikers, responding to medical emergencies, and protecting communities from fast-moving brush fires, LA City Park Rangers never know what their next call will bring. With approximately 30 active rangers responsible for more than 450 parks across Los Angeles, their work requires courage, compassion, and a deep commitment to public service.

Go on patrol with the men and women who protect some of L.A.’s most treasured natural spaces. Hear about the split-second decisions they make, the dangers they face, and the calling that keeps them coming back—even after routine encounters turn into life-threatening situations.

Whether they are helping someone through the worst day of their life, teaching children about the parks or preserving L.A.’s remaining wildlands for future generations, these rangers wear many hats. Their mission is simple but powerful: protect the parks, preserve the environment and make sure everyone can enjoy these remarkable spaces safely.

For these dedicated public servants, Los Angeles is more than the city they patrol—it is their home, their community and the place they are proud to protect.

#LACityParks

title: Regular City Council-  01/22/99
Join SDPD's Retired Senior Patrol Volunteers!
description:
Getting it done! 👏 For the last year, San Diego Police have leveraged the department’s Retired Senior Patrol Volunteers (RSVPs) to help screen some reports of illegal encampments or illegally parked vehicles. These volunteers are checking reports made through the Get It Done system and helping triage them to the appropriate City department to address it. 

If the encampment is still active with people living there, the City will begin the process to address their needs and eventually clean up the encampment. If the encampment is abandoned, then the report is routed for the City to clean the area. Using RSVPs to help review some of the reports saves time, money and ultimately keeps officers available to respond to the community.

SDPD is looking for more volunteers! ⭐ Assisting with Get-It-Done reports is just part of the important work these volunteers do. More info: sandiego.gov/volunteer-program/opportunities/police#rsvp

title: After 7 Years, This LA Splash Pad Is Back!
description:
After being closed for more than seven summers, the Panorama City Park splash pad is officially back, bringing smiles, laughter, and much-needed relief to families in one of Los Angeles' most densely populated neighborhoods.

Community members, City leaders, and nearly 200 families gathered to celebrate the grand reopening of the free splash pad, a long-awaited investment that provides local children with a safe place to play and cool off during the summer heat.

The reopening is also a story of community advocacy. Inspired by a simple question from her son about why the splash pad had been closed, one Panorama City resident worked with her children, neighbors, and local leaders to push for change. Their persistence helped spark the effort to restore the splash pad, proving that community voices—no matter their age—can make a real difference.

For more information about the City of Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks programs, visit: https://recreation.parks.lacity.gov/

description:
This week’s Blue Notebook (May 3-9) has a little bit of everything: goodbyes, hellos, traffic stops, graffiti arrests, outreach updates, a 5K, an award, and a reminder to be kind. Basically, a full SMPD group chat in video form.

Highlights:

🚔 Crime Suppression
2528 calls for service and 106 arrests, including the recovery of a child involved in an abduction and 4 arrests tied to active graffiti tagging. A handgun was also recovered.

🏍️ Traffic Safety
472 traffic stops, 305 citations, motorcycle safety operations, and 76 voluntary breath test demos during our “Know Your Limits” DUI education campaign. Because traffic safety is not just about tickets. It is about keeping people alive.

🤝 Homeless Outreach
153 radio calls, 138 self-initiated contacts, 10 arrests, 27 citations, and 7 encampments addressed. Officers also used a mobile fingerprint reader to identify a person who provided a false name and was wanted for felony probation violation.

🌟 Community Engagement
We stopped by the Rick Crocker 5K Challenge, celebrated Officer Anthony Angel’s recognition from the Santa Monica-Malibu PTA, and shared details about the Downtown Substation ribbon cutting on May 28 at noon.

Also: Cadet Alexis signs off, Cadet Naomi steps in, and yes, Sgt. Rick still manages to keep the whole thing moving.

Watch the full episode and, as always, choose kindness. A small gesture can brighten someone’s day.

title: Arts, Parks, Libraries, and Community Enrichment Committee - SAP  - 1/27/26
Earn While You Learn: How Angeleno Corps Changes Lives in LA
description:
What is Angeleno Corps?

Angeleno Corps is a 10-month City of Los Angeles program that gives young adults ages 18 to 30 the opportunity to gain real-world work experience while serving their communities.

The program places 350 participants with more than 50 community-based organizations across six service areas: education and child care; health, climate and environmental justice; immigration assistance; nutrition and food justice; technology and digital assistance; and housing rights advocacy.

Participants receive a $1,000 monthly stipend, individualized mentorship, professional development training, and support through the City’s YouthSource Centers. Corps members must also be enrolled full-time in a post-secondary education program.

By combining education with hands-on community service, Angeleno Corps helps young adults build professional skills, gain valuable experience, and explore potential career paths while making an impact across Los Angeles.

Learn more at https://hirelayouth.com/

title: A Jumpstart at Careers in Public Service!
description:
Giving young people a jumpstart at careers in public service! 🌟Our successful Employ & Empower internship program has been renewed for another year.

Employ & Empower will continue to be funded by Youth Services Corps, a statewide program within the Office of the Governor’s California Volunteers and will have no impact on the current or projected City budget for next year.

Check out sandiego.gov/Employ-Empower/About to learn more and find out how to apply!

title: Trade, Travel, and Tourism Committee - SAP - 06/09/2026
City of San Diego Prepares for Rain
description:
More rain is on the way to San Diego, and we’re getting ready. 🌧️ 

Rain is expected over the next few days and possibly into the weekend. City of San Diego crews are preparing by inspecting storm drains, pump stations, channels and other stormwater infrastructure. San Diego Fire-Rescue's Lifeguard swiftwater rescue teams are pre-positioned across the City. 

Before the rain, residents can take a few simple steps: 
- Sweep and pick up trash, leaves, grass clippings and other debris that collect around storm drains and curb gutters near your home.
- Proactively turn off irrigation to save water and minimize runoff. 
- Know the safest routes to and from your home or property should flooding occur. 
- SLOW DOWN and do not drive, ride or walk through flood waters. 

To report storm-related issues, like flooding or fallen branches, report them on the Get It Done app or call 619-527-7500. If you have an emergency, dial 911.

#SanDiego #storm #rain

title: Ambulance Operator Program
description:
The Santa Monica Fire Department launched its new in-house Ambulance Operator Program on Feb. 1, part of the city’s two-year Realignment Plan. The program establishes a dedicated team responsible for safely operating ambulances and supporting paramedic teams during emergency medical responses.

Previously, emergency medical transport was handled by a third-party provider. With this program, the Fire Department now provides these services using in-house personnel, vehicles and equipment, helping improve response efficiency across the community.

The program is projected to generate approximately $7 million in new revenue while strengthening emergency medical services for Santa Monica residents.

title: What happens to your trash?
description:
What happens to your trash after it leaves your curbside bin? Hear from City of San Diego Biologist Burton Ewert about how refuse is compacted throughout the day as part of the City's maintenance of the Miramar Landfill. 

Facts: 
• Nearly 910,000 tons of trash are disposed of annually.
• Spans more than 1,500 acres and is the City's only active landfill.
• Opened Dec. 7, 1959.
• Methane - a greenhouse gas produced as a byproduct of waste decomposition  - is captured and used to provide 90% of the fuel to power electrical generators at the Metropolitan Biosolids Center.

title: Planning and Land Use Management Committee - 10/28/25
Explore the Japanese Garden: A Hidden Gem in Los Angeles
description:
Discover one of Los Angeles' best-kept secrets.

The Japanese Garden is a 6.5-acre oasis in the San Fernando Valley, featuring tranquil lakes, authentic Japanese landscapes, and peaceful walking paths that make it an ideal destination for visitors of all ages. Whether you're looking for a relaxing stroll or a unique cultural experience, this hidden gem offers a serene escape from the city's hustle and bustle.

Recent enhancements include a new dry Zen garden, renovated pathways, new bridges, and refreshed visitor facilities, making the garden more beautiful than ever.

The garden also celebrates Japanese culture through its monthly Japanese Cultural Program, held on the second Sunday of each month. Visitors can enjoy activities and demonstrations such as taiko drumming, origami, kimono presentations, and other traditional arts. 

Learn more about visiting the Japanese Garden, including hours, admission, and upcoming cultural programs: https://thejapanesegarden.com/

Inside the Koreatown Media Lab: FREE Help to Start or Grow Your Business!
description:
Are you a small business owner or thinking about starting a business? Turn your ideas into action with free, one-on-one small business counseling at the Pio Pico–Koreatown Branch Library.

On the second Thursday of each month, experienced counselors from PACE—the Pacific Asian Consortium in Employment—offer free 30-minute consultations for aspiring entrepreneurs and established business owners. Participants can receive personalized guidance on starting or growing a business, financing, permits, licensing, marketing and other operational challenges. Counselors can also provide continued support based on each participant’s needs.

Entrepreneurs can also explore the Koreatown Media Lab, which features modern equipment for designing posters, creating 3D prints, producing business logos and bringing creative projects to life.

These free City resources make professional guidance and business tools more accessible, helping local entrepreneurs succeed while strengthening Los Angeles’ small-business community.

Check the Pio Pico–Koreatown Branch Library calendar for upcoming counseling sessions and workshops.

title: Foster Youth Celebrate Graduation at Sea World San Diego
description:
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Tacos and penguins and sloths, oh my! County Child and Family Well Being brought joy, celebration and accomplishment to local foster youth and teens enrolled in the Independent Living Skills program during a splashy high school graduation event at SeaWorld San Diego.  

Nearly 200 graduates, family members and supporters attended the June 26 event to honor and cheer on 70 foster youth who earned their high school diplomas. For many, graduation marks not just an academic milestone, but a moment of resilience and triumph over challenges that can make educational success hard to achieve.

Little Tokyo came alive with Japanese culture, community, and summer fun at the Japanese American National Museum’s (JANM) annual Natsumatsuri Family Festival!

Held Saturday, August 15, 2026, at Terasaki Budokan in Little Tokyo, Los Angeles, the free celebration welcomed families and visitors of all backgrounds for traditional Obon dancing, live music, civic pop-ups, and hands-on cultural activities.

Although JANM’s main building is temporarily closed for renovations, the museum kept this cherished tradition going by bringing the festival to the nearby Terasaki Budokan. Natsumatsuri proved that community spirit is not tied to a single building—it thrives wherever people gather to celebrate culture, history and one another.

title: LA Metro Unveils Major New App and Tap-to-Pay System
description:
Los Angeles Metro has launched its first-ever official rider app, giving Angelenos a smarter and more personalized way to navigate the city. 

The app helps users plan trips with real-time bus, rail, and bike options, while learning daily travel patterns, such as regular commutes to work or school, to tailor the experience around the routes they use most. Riders can also quickly locate amenities like bathrooms, bike lockers, and TAP retailers.

Metro is also modernizing payments, allowing riders to tap and pay with physical or digital credit and debit cards across Metro and 26 participating regional transit agencies. While these improvements arrive ahead of the FIFA World Cup, they are part of a much larger effort to transform the transit experience for everyday riders, visitors, and the millions expected for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games.

title: ¡Viva México! Thousands Gather for an Unforgettable El Grito Tradition
description:
On September 15, 2026, thousands of Angelenos gathered at Los Angeles City Hall to celebrate El Grito de Dolores with pride, passion, and tradition. The annual event commemorates the call that launched Mexico’s struggle for independence while honoring the rich history and contributions of Los Angeles’ Mexican and Mexican American communities.

For many families, the evening was an opportunity to honor the sacrifices of previous generations and encourage younger generations to embrace their heritage with pride.

Home to one of the largest populations of Mexican descent outside of Mexico, Los Angeles welcomed people from across the city to take part in the celebration. The event highlighted a cultural legacy that remains vibrant, resilient, and deeply connected to the city’s identity.

As joyful cheers of “¡Viva México!” echoed through the crowd, the celebration reflected the enduring strength and spirit of Los Angeles’ Mexican and Mexican American communities.

description:
Slurry seal is like giving our streets a tune‑up. Just as regular car maintenance helps the engine last longer, slurry seal helps extend the life of our roads without the cost of full reconstruction. 

Slurry seal provides a waterproof barrier that seals the asphalt by adding a fresh layer of highly textured aggregates that halt harmful oxidation. This cost-effective treatment keeps neighborhoods in good shape for years to come.

This work was recently completed on Cole Street in Clairemont.

title: New Bike Lanes and Safer Roads Debut in Griffith Park
description:
After years of community advocacy and efforts to prevent future traffic tragedies, Griffith Park's largest-ever safety improvement project is officially complete.

City leaders, community advocates, and residents gathered in Griffith Park to celebrate the opening of new bike lanes and major safety improvements along Crystal Springs Drive and Zoo Drive.

Representing the largest safety investment in Griffith Park's history, the project was made possible through a $4 million state earmark secured by former California Assembly Member Laura Friedman. Improvements include newly repaved roadways, dedicated space for cyclists and pedestrians, and traffic-calming measures designed to reduce cut-through traffic and improve safety for all park users.

The project was shaped by years of community advocacy following several serious traffic incidents, including the 2022 hit-and-run death of cyclist Andrew Jelmert and a near-fatal hit-and-run crash in 2013 that inspired the creation of Streets Are For Everyone.

title: Free Eyeglasses Give Hundreds of Pacoima Families a Brighter Future
description:
Nearly one in three Los Angeles students needs glasses to succeed in school. To tackle this urgent need, local partners recently hosted a free vision clinic in Pacoima, delivering immediate relief to hundreds of local residents.

The Power of Sight Foundation teamed up with Ketchum Health University, Councilwoman Monica Rodriguez, and Real 92.3 to transform local healthcare access. Dedicated families lined up to receive free eye exams, fresh meals, and back-to-school backpacks.

Unlike traditional clinics, technicians crafted custom prescription glasses on-site, allowing every patient to walk home with brand-new eyewear the very same day.

For many adults and children, this event marked their first eye exam ever. High costs and limited insurance often put vision care out of reach for neighborhood families. By bringing these vital services directly to Pacoima, organizers removed major financial hurdles and gave community members the tools they need to thrive.

Isang mahalagang mensahe mula sa DPSS tungkol sa Federal Government Shutdown
description:
Kung tumatanggap ka ng mga benepisyo ng CalFresh, malamang na narinig mo na ang tungkol sa kasalukuyang pagsasara ng pamahalaang pederal at ang epekto nito sa iyong mga benepisyo ng CalFresh.

Narito ang kailangan mong malaman:
• Ang pagsasara ay nangangahulugan na ang pamahalaang pederal ay hindi papahintulutan ang mga benepisyo ng CalFresh para sa buwan ng Nobyembre 2025. 
• Kapag natapos na ang pagsasara, ang mga benepisyo ay ibibigay sa mga naging karapat-dapat sa buwan ng Nobyembre.
• Kung ang iyong CalFresh SAR 7 o taunang pag-renew ay nakatakda na sa panahon ng pagsasara, DAPAT mong kumpletuhin na ang mga ito upang manatiling karapat-dapat na patuloy mong matatanggap ang iyong mga benepisyo kapag natapos na ang pagsasara.

Hinihikayat ka naming bisitahin ang iyong lokal na food pantry at kumonekta sa iyong mga lokal na samahan ng organisasyon para sa tulong sa panahong ito na mahirap.

Para sa listahan ng mga lokasyon, mangyaring bisitahin ang LAFoodBank.org o makipag-ugnayan sa 211 sa pamamagitan ng pag-dial ng 2-1-1 o pabisita sa www.211.org.

​👮‍♀️ A Look Inside the Badge: Sgt. Elaina Hassan & K9 Jack's Story (Thanksgiving Special)

​This Thanksgiving week, we're taking a moment to celebrate the family that supports our Santa Monica Police Department (SMPD) and introducing you to one of our finest: Sergeant Elaina Hassan.

​In this exclusive interview, Sgt. Hassan opens up about her journey: from her college days and early career in Arizona to finding her true professional home here at the SMPD. She shares what inspired her to serve and the powerful role her family plays in her demanding career.

​🌟 What You'll See in This Video:
​The Journey to SMPD: Hear about her well-rounded background, including her education in Arizona, and why she chose to join the Santa Monica Police Department.

​The Passion for Travel: Discover Sgt. Hassan's love for exploring and how that broad perspective informs her work in our community.

​More Than a Partner: Hear the heartwarming story of her bond with K9 Jack, and why he is truly considered part of her immediate family.

​We are incredibly grateful for the dedication of Sgt. Hassan, K9 Jack, and the entire SMPD team. Wishing everyone in our community a safe and happy holiday!

title: Một thông báo quan trọng từ Sở DPSS về việc Chính Phủ Liên Bang Đóng Cửa
description:
Nếu quý vị đang nhận phúc lợi CalFresh, quý vị có thể đã nghe về việc chính phủ liên bang hiện đang đóng cửa và tác động của việc đóng cửa liên quan đến phúc lợi CalFresh của quý vị.

Sau đây là những điều quý vị cần biết:
• Việc chính phủ đóng cửa đồng nghĩa với việc chính phủ liên bang sẽ không cấp phúc lợi CalFresh cho Tháng Mười Một, 2025.
• Sau khi việc đóng cửa chính phủ kết thúc, phúc lợi sẽ được cấp cho những người đủ-điều-kiện trong tháng Mười Một.
• Nếu mẫu SAR 7 hoặc đơn xin-gia-hạn CalFresh hàng năm của quý vị đến hạn trong thời gian chính phủ đóng cửa, quý vị PHẢI hoàn thành đúng hạn để vẫn đủ điều kiện và có thể tiếp tục nhận được phúc lợi của mình sau khi chính phủ hoạt động trở lại.
Chúng tôi khuyến khích quý vị đến các kho thực phẩm tại địa phương của mình và kết nối với các tổ chức tương trợ tại địa phương để được hỗ trợ trong thời điểm khó khăn này.

Để  xem danh sách các địa điểm, xin quý vị truy cập trang mạng LAFoodBank.org hoặc liên lạc 211 bằng cách gọi số 2-1-1 hoặc truy cập trang mạng www.211.org.
