title: Trade, Travel and Tourism Committee - 10/28/2025
Businesses Urged to Prepare for El Niño
description:
As part of the City's broader El Niño preparedness efforts, Economic Development Department teams will be visiting businesses over a span of six weeks in areas with a history of flooding – including Barrio Logan, Encanto, Logan Heights, Southcrest, Pacific Beach, Mission Beach and Ocean Beach – to share tips on how they can prepare. They are also collaborating with business associations to help share emergency and preparedness information. Economic Development Department staff expect to visit approximately 1,500 businesses through October.

Stormwater drainage systems in the public right of way are designed for typical rain events. An excessive amount of rain, especially in a short period of time, could overwhelm the City’s stormwater system and cause flooding. Because these conditions have the potential to impact communities across the city, including some business districts, it is critical to understand the risks and take steps to prepare.

#StayReadySanDiego #CityofSanDiego #BusinessWalks

Protect Your Home: Reducing Wildfire Risk Starts with Zone 0
description: Beginning in February 2026, the City of San Diego will implement Zone 0, a new California defensible space law. Zone 0 requires property owners to remove combustible materials, including trash, debris, and certain vegetation, within 0 to 5 feet of structures located in the City’s Very High Fire Severity Zones. This area is critical for helping reduce the risk of fires caused by wind-driven embers. Learn more at SanDiego.gov/DefensibleSpace.

#LACounty Close Up: Episode 283 Promo
Afro-Latino Culture Takes Center Stage in Los Angeles
description:
What started with 20 people in a backyard has grown into an event expected to welcome more than 2,000 attendees. The Fourth Annual Afro-Latino Culture Fest, described by organizers as the only festival of its kind on the West Coast, celebrates Afro-Latino identity, heritage, and culture.

The festival brings together Afro-Latino communities with roots in Puerto Rico, Cuba, Panama, and other parts of Latin America and the Caribbean. The event features live performances, educational programming, food vendors, music, dancing, art, and opportunities for community and business connections.

Organizers say the festival provides a dedicated space for Afro-Latinos to celebrate their African and Latin American heritage while highlighting their historical and cultural contributions. It also addresses the importance of representation for people who identify as both Black and Latino.

With more than 40,000 Afro-Latinos living in the Los Angeles area, the festival offers attendees an opportunity to connect through shared cultures and experiences while learning more about the diversity of the broader Latino community.

title: Los Angeles Honors Jewish American Heritage Month Champions in Sports
description:
During the 2026 Jewish American Heritage Month celebrations, the City of Los Angeles paid tribute to several honorees under this year's theme "Playing It Forward: Championing Jewish Values in Sports."

Honorees included actor Eric Braeden, best known for an ongoing role on the TV series "The Young and the Restless," who played soccer with the Maccabee Los Angeles team in the 1970s. Braeden shared that his experience on the team taught him to stand up to prejudice. 

Another honoree Mitch Gaylord was the first gymnast in history to score a perfect ten during the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games.

Pro hockey player honoree Chelsey Goldberg highlighted how faith and sport can combine to inspire resilience, bring people together, and build community.

title: Installing upgraded stormwater infrastructure
description:
City of San Diego crews are hard at work in Rolando Village installing upgraded stormwater infrastructure to protect homes and streets ahead of a strong predicted El Niño rainy season. 

Infrastructure improvements happen year-round thanks to the Stormwater Department’s dedicated in-house engineering, repair and maintenance teams. This work is crucial to making San Diego neighborhoods more flood-resilient. 

Residents can also prepare ahead of the rainy season. For tips on preparing your home, visit the City’s storm preparedness page: sandiego.gov/storm-preparedness.

Calling all Swifties! New Romantics, Los Angeles' Taylor Swift tribute band, takes the stage on Sunday, August 2 for a family-friendly performance featuring hits from every era, with 101 Girls opening the show.

title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) February 5, 2026 Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) meeting of February 5, 2026 highlighted the alarming number of in custody deaths reported in 2026 and reinforced the SBCs mandate to monitor jail conditions and pursue accountability.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) reported out on meals, water quality, food waste, and facility equipment postponed to March 2026, limiting immediate insight into key operational areas. A discussion ensued with District Attorney Nathan Hochman on the handling of sexual assault allegations involving deputies, systemic failures in facilities such as the Century Regional Detention Facility (CRDF), and the deteriorating conditions of Men’s Central Jail (MCJ). Hochman expressed support for the SBC’s oversight role and affirmed the DA’s commitment to independent investigation of misconduct, while also noting the ongoing need for structural reform and facility replacement.

The SBC raised concerns about violence, retaliation, Title 15 violations, and lack of transparency, particularly regarding the so called “cop shop” allegations. And the necessity of obtaining consistent corrective action plan (CAP) responses and strengthening inter agency cooperation.

The LASD’s Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) Coordinator, explained complaint intake, investigative pathways, and the roles of specialized units. Despite these updates, the SBC underscored the need for robust accountability measures and clearer communication from LASDs leadership.

City of San Diego & USS Midway Museum Unveil Newest City Street - “Midway Place”
description: The USS Midway Museum and the City of San Diego, partners for more than 20 years, have been working together for several months on the new “Midway Place” street in downtown San Diego. The new street is a tribute to the USS Midway for its nearly 50 years of active-duty service with the U.S. Navy and its more than two decades as a floating naval ship museum in San Diego. The street will be officially christened by the unveiling of the new street sign that will recognize the service and sacrifice of the nearly 200,000 sailors who served on board the Midway from 1945-1992 and acknowledge Midway Museum as one of San Diego’s most iconic symbols. Midway, the world’s most popular and visited naval ship museum, is the “#1 Thing To Do in San Diego” as per Tripadvisor. More than 21 million guests have visited Midway since opening as a museum in 2004.

title: A Lifeline for Recovery: L.A. Opens 96-Bed Care Facility
description:
A brand-new care center in Los Angeles is opening its doors to help local residents rebuild their lives. The Restorative Care Village has officially launched its newest phase, adding 96 recuperative beds and vital health services to the neighborhood.

The newly expanded facility features an urgent care center, mental health rehabilitation units, and a 24-hour withdrawal management space. Patients will receive round-the-clock medical assistance, professional counseling, and long-term recovery planning designed to help them safely stabilize.

This powerful initiative was created directly with local community input. Neighbors helped design the layout and color scheme to ensure the space feels welcoming and supportive. Community leaders believe this facility will serve as a vital lifeline and a true entryway into lasting recovery for those who need it most.

Circular SoCal: A Catalyst for a Regenerative Future Highlight Video
description:
Link to the full event: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cn76Lby6cF0

City of Santa Monica, Carbon Leadership Forum – Los Angeles, and AIA Los Angeles held an expert-level conversation on circularity in the built environment discussing how to become a catalyst for change, driving tangible collaboration and innovation across all scales.

* Become Part of the Solution: Dive deep into the principles of the circular economy with top architects, designers, policymakers, and sustainability leaders. An opportunity to co-create a more resilient, regenerative future for our region.
* Unlock Collaboration: Explore how to build pathways from material innovation to policy transformation, identifying barriers and collectively unlocking obstacles. Hands-on, table-based workshops to develop short-, medium-, and long-term goals.
* Hear from the Experts: Featuring a welcome from the Mayor of Santa Monica and three expert panels covering the material, building, and municipal scales. Gain crucial insights into innovative building codes, product-as-a-service models, and strategies for deconstruction ordinances.
* Connect with Leaders: Networking with a diverse and influential group of attendees, including architects, urban planners, policymakers, developers, and sustainability professionals, all committed to advancing the circular economy.

Beneath Los Angeles Lies a 50,000-Year-Old Ice Age Time Capsule
description:
Beneath the streets of Los Angeles lies one of the world's most remarkable Ice Age fossil sites. For tens of thousands of years, the La Brea Tar Pits have preserved an extraordinary record of prehistoric life, including saber-tooth cats, dire wolves, mammoths, mastodons, American lions, and ancient camels.

The site sits above an oil field where petroleum naturally migrates to the surface through fractures in the ground. These asphalt seeps trapped and preserved plants and animals over thousands of years, creating one of the largest and most diverse collections of Ice Age fossils ever discovered. Scientific excavations have been ongoing since 1906, with millions of specimens recovered from the site. More recently, excavations associated with nearby development projects have uncovered more than one million additional fossils, expanding a collection that continues to fuel new discoveries.

Today, excavations are carefully monitored by paleontologists, archaeologists, and Native American representatives to ensure that fossils and cultural resources are documented and recovered responsibly. The museum is scheduled to close on July 7 for a two-year renovation project, with fossils temporarily displayed at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County and a mobile museum continuing educational outreach. When it reopens as the Samuel Oschin Global Center for Ice Age Research, visitors will be able to see millions of fossils and observe scientists at work in open laboratories as they study one of the most important windows into Ice Age life anywhere in the world.

The Museum at La Brea Tar Pits is temporarily closed for construction. 
Many outdoor areas of Hancock Park remain open. 
Learn more here: https://tarpits.org/

title: The Nisei Parade Brings the Spirit of Japan to Los Angeles!
description:
Japanese culture takes center stage as the Nisei Parade fills the streets with music, dancing, tradition, and community pride.

Celebrating Nisei—the second generation of Japanese Americans—the family-friendly event honors the history and contributions of Japanese American families while bringing people from all backgrounds together. Attendees enjoy authentic Japanese food, cultural performances and traditional displays, including Matoi and Mando, accompanied by drums, bells and flutes.

For participants and spectators, the annual parade offers a meaningful connection to Japan and an opportunity to experience the rich Japanese culture found throughout Los Angeles.

title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) January 8, 2026 Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) meeting of January 8, 2026, reviewed key operational conditions within Los Angeles County correctional facilities. Updates focused on improvements to food services, sanitation and water safety, digital access expansion, and custodial staffing stability. The Commission also received a detailed report on in custody deaths for 2025, noting 46 total deaths and ongoing tracking into 2026.

A significant portion of the meeting centered on serious Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) related sexual misconduct allegations at CRDF, including reports of cross-gender viewing of showers, harassment, and forced acts. Commissioners emphasized the urgency of transparency and corrective action. Requests were made for detailed reports, including Century Regional Detention Facility (CRDF) inspection findings and participation from both Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD’s) PREA Coordinator and District Attorney Nathan Hochman.

Overall, the Commission prioritized accountability, facility safety, and immediate follow up on allegations of staff misconduct.

World's Largest Pop-up Book on Display at LA's Central Library
description:
It’s not just a book—it’s the world’s largest pop-up book right here in Los Angeles!

Created to celebrate the centennial of the Los Angeles Central Library, the monumental Luceros y Penumbras, meaning “Starlight and Shadows,” transforms the library’s Rotunda into a larger-than-life storybook experience.

Featuring artwork conceived by Los Angeles artist and printmaker Daniel González, the installation was designed to rekindle the childhood excitement of opening a pop-up book while inviting visitors to reflect on the role libraries have played in their lives.

Constructing a book of this extraordinary size required industrial-strength cardboard and innovative engineering. Because the fully assembled book was too large to pass through the library’s doors, it had to be designed in smaller sections, transported to the second floor, and carefully reassembled inside the Rotunda.

The spectacular installation officially earned Guinness World Records certification as the world’s largest pop-up book.

ប្រសិនបើអ្នកទទួលបានអត្ថប្រយោជន៍ពីកម្មវិធី CalFresh, អ្នកប្រហែលជាបានដឹងអំពីការផ្អាកដំណើរការនៃស្ថាប័នរដ្ឋាភិបាលសហព័ន្ធក្នុងពេលបច្ចុប្បន្ននេះ ហើយដែលវាបានប៉ះពាល់ទៅលើអត្ថប្រយោជន៍កម្មវិធី CalFresh របស់អ្នក។
នេះគឺជាអ្វីដែលអ្នកត្រូវតែដឹង:
• ការផ្អាកដំណើរការនេះមានន័យថាស្ថាប័នរដ្ឋាភិបាលសហព័ន្ធ នឹងមិនព្រមអត្ថប្រយោជន៍កម្មវិធី CalFresh សម្រាប់ខែវិច្ឆិកា ឆ្នាំ2025 នេះទេ។ 
• នៅពេលដែលការផ្អាកដំណើរការនាៗត្រូវបានបញ្ចប់អត្ថប្រយោជន៍នឹងត្រូវបានផ្តល់ជូនដល់អ្នកដែលមានសិទ្ធិទទួលបាន នៅខែវិច្ឆិកា។
• ប្រសិនបើរបាយការណ៍ពាក់កណ្តាលឆ្នាំ (SAR 7) ឬការកំណត់ពេលទទួលជំនួយឡើងវិញប្រចាំឆ្នាំសំរាប់កម្មវិធី CalFresh របស់អ្នក ត្រូវដល់ពេលកំណត់ក្នុងអំឡុងពេលនៃការផ្អាកដំណើរការនៃស្ថាប័នរដ្ឋាភិបាលសហព័ន្ធ អ្នកត្រូវតែបំពេញកិច្ចការទាំងនោះតាមពេលកំណត់ ដើម្បីបន្តមានសិទ្ធិទទួលជំនួយ ដូច្នេះអ្នកអាចបន្តទទួលបានអត្ថប្រយោជន៍របស់អ្នក បន្ទាប់ពីការផ្អាកដំណើរការនៃស្ថាប័នសហព័ន្ធ ត្រូវបានបញ្ចប់។
យើងសូមជំរុញអោយអ្នកអញ្ជើញទៅកាន់ឃ្លាំងបរិច្ចាកម្ហូបអាហារប្រចាំតំបន់របស់អ្នក ហើយដើម្បីភ្ជាប់ទំនាក់ទំនងជាមួយអង្គការជំនួយរួមនៅក្នុងតំបន់របស់អ្នក សំរាប់ជំនួយក្នុងអំឡុងពេលដ៏លំបាកនេះ។

title: County Breaks Ground on New Children's Crisis Residential Care Facility
description:
The County of San Diego broke ground today on a new Children’s Crisis Residential Care facility in Kearny Mesa that will be a first of its kind locally and fill a critical gap in the children’s system of care. 

The construction involves a full remodel of an existing 10,000‑square‑foot building and will be complete in late 2027. When the facility opens in early 2028, local youth experiencing a behavioral health crisis will have access to a welcoming and supportive 24/7 treatment center. 

The Behavioral Health Services Children’s Crisis Residential Care (CCRC) facility will operate as a short-term residential program. Once operational, the CCRC is expected to offer up to 16 beds and serve approximately 350 youth and families each year. 

As a regional resource, the CCRC will expand local capacity for children’s crisis care and support equitable access to essential behavioral health care by serving Medi-Cal eligible children and youth.  

Services will include timely mental health assessments, individualized treatment, stabilization and warm hand-offs to ongoing care. The purpose is to reduce unnecessary transfers and keep children connected to the support they need. 

The $12 million County infrastructure investment is funded largely through the Behavioral Health Continuum Infrastructure Program (BHCIP) along with other federal and state grants.

Class three e-bikes already require individuals to be 16 years or older to operate.

title: Regular City Council - 6/5/26
Need a Job, Housing, or Medical Care? Start at the LA Public Library
description:
The Los Angeles Public Library is much more than books—it is a place where Angelenos can connect with vital information, assistance, and community resources.

The Source at Central Library brings service providers together in one convenient location on the last Tuesday of every month from 12:30 to 3:00 p.m. Visitors can receive help accessing free phones, birth certificates, medical care, Medi-Cal resources, employment services, job training, housing assistance, transportation support, and more.

Participating organizations include Step Up on Second, The Midnight Mission, Homeboy Industries, and other local service providers offering support for people experiencing homelessness, health challenges, employment barriers, and other needs. Assistance is available in several community languages, including Spanish, Chinese, Thai and American Sign Language.

Visitors can also use the library’s air conditioning, restrooms, and phone-charging stations while learning about services they may not have known were available.

📅 Last Tuesday of every month
🕧 12:30–3:00 p.m.
📍 Los Angeles Central Library
630 W. Fifth St., Los Angeles, CA 90071

Want to explore available programs? Go to https://www.lapl.org/.

title: Youth Transition Campus Helps Students Build Skills and Succeed in School
description:
County Probation and the San Diego County Office of Education are partnering to help justice‑involved youth build stronger futures. At the Youth Transition Campus and East Mesa Juvenile Detention Facility, students earn a full high school education and can take online college courses that help them stay on track academically.

Beyond core classes, students can choose Career Technical Education (CTE) courses that teach practical, real‑world job skills. These programs give youth tools they can use when they return to their communities and prepare them for the workforce.

title: San Carlos Affordable Housing Project Breaks Ground on 44 New Homes
description: Forty-four individuals and families, including those with intellectual or developmental disabilities, will soon have a new place to call home in San Carlos. On Tuesday, June 16, Mayor Todd Gloria and City staff joined Community HousingWorks and other local leaders to celebrate the groundbreaking of the Navajo Family Apartments located at 7005 Navajo Road. The one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments will be affordable to households making 30% to 70% of the area median income. Project-based vouchers allow rental assistance to be attached to a specific unit and/or project instead of to an eligible assisted family.

Transportation Agencies Breakdown World Cup Performance 8/26/2026
description:
Los Angeles is racing against the clock to build a transportation system capable of moving millions of people during the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

During a congressional panel in West Hollywood, federal lawmakers and regional transportation leaders examined lessons from the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the challenges that remain before LA28. Metro’s enhanced World Cup bus service provided more than 212,000 rides to and from SoFi Stadium, offering an important preview of the planning, coordination and public-safety measures required for a global sporting event.

The discussion addressed the need for approximately 1,700 additional buses, billions of dollars in federal support and greater coordination among Metro, LADOT, municipal transit agencies and public-safety partners. Officials also discussed traffic congestion, first- and last-mile connections, accessibility, bicycle parking, rideshare services, neighborhood impacts and the need to protect everyday transit service for local residents.

Leaders emphasized that transportation investments made for LA28 should create lasting benefits—including safer streets, improved bus stops, better mobility infrastructure and new economic opportunities—for communities across the Los Angeles region.

title: Kinship Program: Foster Youth Thrive When They Live with Family
description:
In San Diego County, 1,074 children are currently in foster care, and nearly half—531—are living with relatives. Placing children with family members is the County’s preferred option.

Kinship care places a child full-time with extended family or close family friends instead of an unrelated caregivers or group setting. These placements often begin as soon as the child enters foster care and may last weeks, months or even years.

The County’s Child and Family Well‑Being (CFWB) department prioritizes kinship placements whenever possible. Research shows foster youth who live with family experience greater stability and less trauma than those placed in non-relative settings. Kinship care is linked to better  long-term behavioral and mental health outcomes, as well as higher academic achievement.

Living with relatives also helps children stay connected to their culture, community and siblings while they work toward healing and, when possible, reunification with their parents.

Many kinship caregivers – especially grandparents living on fixed incomes – take on this responsibility with limited resources. To support them, the County offers them financial, legal, educational and community assistance to help ensure their families remain stable and successful.

It has made a real difference for Jean, Oscar and Valerie — and for so many families across our region who open their homes and their hearts to keep children safe, supported and connected to the people who love them.

title: Regular City Council - 01/26/99
County Animal Services Caring for Animals Rescued from Julian Property
description:
On May 1, County Animal Services, the San Diego Humane Society and several other shelters and rescue groups partnered to remove hundreds of animals from a Julian property where they were not receiving proper care.

County Animal Services took in dozens of the rescued animals, including several farm animals.

On May 15, the Humane Farming Association transported two pigs, all rescued goats and several chickens in need of ongoing medical care from the County’s Bonita shelter. The organization sent a specialized trailer and transport team all the way from Minnesota.

“Animal welfare is something that needs every single one of us to be a part of,” said Dr. Brie Sarvis, director and chief veterinarian. “We are only better when we work together.”

The animals were taken to a rescue organization that specializes in caring for farm animals, giving them the chance to live in a safer, healthier environment.

For more details, visit the San Diego Humane Society’s Julian Rescue page: https://sdhumane.org/about/media-center/emergency-updates/emergency-rescue/

County Animal Services promotes the humane and responsible care of pets by providing the unincorporated areas of San Diego County with 24-hour animal rescues; helping those who can no longer care for their pets; investigating and stopping animal cruelty or neglect; enforcing state and local laws related to animals as needed; and educating the public about responsible care, which includes animal welfare, restraint and licensing benefits.

title: City Council Meeting SAP - 5/5/26
Additional Affordable Housing Headed to South Bay
description:
An outdated motel in Chula Vista will soon be transformed into new affordable housing. 
 
Palomar Point broke ground today at 1160 Walnut Avenue, the site of the former Palomar Motel, to begin renovations on 27 new permanent supportive housing units.  
 
The apartment homes are for individuals experiencing homelessness with 7 units designated for unhoused veterans. Residents will have access to a case manager and activities coordinator to support their health and independence and offer services tailored to their individual needs.  
 
Managed by Wakeland Housing and Community Development Corp, the rehabilitation project will convert each motel room into a studio apartment with a kitchenette. Renovations include new flooring, updated fixtures, a new roof, upgraded plumbing, electrical and HVAC systems, fire sprinklers, accessibility improvements and stairway replacements. 

The Palomar Point project is made possible through public/private partnerships between the County, the City of Chula Vista and Wakeland Housing.  

The County contributed 27 Section 8 Project Based Vouchers (PBV) through the housing authority. These Project Based Vouchers support the on-going operating costs of the development and have an estimated value of $694,980 annually and $14M over the next 20 years.  

The estimated date of completion and grand reopening is December 2026.  

Visit the Wakeland Housing website (https://www.wakelandhdc.com/) for more information about leasing opportunities. 

Since 2017, the County has invested more than $334 million into affordable housing, using excess land, its Innovative Housing Trust Fund alongside other state, federal, and local funding sources administered by the County. Those funds have helped open doors to over 3,400 homes with 2,600 more on the way.  

The County’s Housing Hub (https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/housing-hub.html) has more information about its efforts to meet the needs of the community.

45th Annual Lotus Festival Celebrates Sri Lankan Culture at Echo Park Lake
description:
Colorful performances, incredible food, and vibrant traditions took over Echo Park Lake as Los Angeles celebrated the 45th Annual Lotus Festival, honoring Sri Lanka as this year's featured host country.

The Lotus Festival is one of Los Angeles' longest-running cultural celebrations, bringing together communities from across the city for a weekend of live performances, traditional dance and music, authentic cuisine, cultural exhibits, and family-friendly activities. This year's festival highlights the rich heritage of Sri Lanka while celebrating the diversity that makes Los Angeles one of the world's most multicultural cities.

Hear from City leaders, community members, and Sri Lankan representatives as they reflect on the importance of preserving cultural traditions, sharing them with future generations, and creating opportunities for Angelenos to learn from one another. From food and entertainment to cultural exchange and community pride, the Lotus Festival showcases how Los Angeles continues to bring people together through shared experiences.

Learn more about the Lotus Festival at:
http://www.lotusfestivalla.com/

Decodable books help children understand the sounds created by different letter combinations, and they can now be found at Central Library’s new “Decode with Odi” section!

title: Get Up Close with Sharks at Cabrillo Marine Aquarium
description:
Celebrate Shark Week at Cabrillo Marine Aquarium, where visitors can dive into the fascinating world of sharks during AZA Shark and Ray Awareness Day. This special event offers a rare chance to explore museum specimens that aren't normally on display, including shark jaws from different species, great white shark vertebrae, and even real shark skin you can touch.

Beyond the special exhibits, Cabrillo Marine Aquarium offers a science-based, hands-on experience for visitors of all ages. Learn about marine life through detailed biological illustrations, discover the anatomy of sharks, octopuses, and other sea creatures, and explore exhibits featuring both common and scientific species names. Guests can also enjoy crafts, activities, giveaways, and educational experiences designed to inspire curiosity about ocean conservation.

Admission to Cabrillo Marine Aquarium is always free, making it an affordable family destination in the Port of Los Angeles. Parking at Cabrillo Beach is available for a fee.

Learn more and plan your visit: https://www.cabrillomarineaquarium.org

The Super Bowl Is Returning to LA!
description:
The Super Bowl is returning to Los Angeles just five years after its last visit. Hosting one of the world’s biggest sporting events brings major benefits to the region, from boosting tourism and supporting local businesses to building excitement and civic pride.

Beyond the economic impact, Los Angeles is also using the event to create more opportunities for local youth. Organizers are expanding access to flag football through programs designed to make participation more affordable and accessible for kids across the region.

By bringing the big game back to Los Angeles, the city is showing young people that there are many ways to be part of the world of sports—whether they dream of playing on the field, working behind the scenes, or reporting on the action.

The Super Bowl may last just one day, but its impact can help support local businesses, strengthen communities, and create new opportunities for the next generation.

Grand Opening of Terrasini, a 95-Unit Affordable Housing Development for Seniors
description:
SAN DIEGO – Chelsea Investment Corporation (Chelsea), County Supervisor Monica Montgomery-Steppe, San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria, and Councilmember Dr. Jennifer Campbell gathered to celebrate the grand opening of Terrasini, a 95-unit affordable housing development for individuals aged 62+.  
Older adults are the fastest-growing population experiencing homelessness in San Diego, often due to job loss or serious illness. They struggle to afford rent on monthly incomes as low as $1,200 and often have to choose between food and medicine. Terrasini will change the quality of life for 95 San Diego seniors who struggle to find a safe and affordable place to call home.

title: See an Abandoned Vehicle in LA? Call 1-800-ABANDON
description:
Abandoned vehicles can block driveways and walkways, create safety hazards, and affect the quality of life in Los Angeles neighborhoods. A new campaign in South Los Angeles is working to clear abandoned and inoperable vehicles from City streets while improving coordination among City departments.

During Fiscal Year 2025–26, the Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT) removed 6,661 abandoned vehicles from City streets. The initiative will increase awareness of the City’s reporting tools and help officials respond more efficiently to vehicles that pose safety or environmental hazards, violate parking regulations or meet other established enforcement criteria.

When a vehicle is being used as a dwelling, LADOT works with partner departments to offer outreach and available services to its occupants before towing.

To report an abandoned vehicle in Los Angeles, call 1-800-ABANDON (1-800-222-6366), Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. After-hours callers may leave a voicemail.

title: Things to Do (for the weekend of September 26th)
description:
Looking for something to do in Los Angeles? From bilingual storytelling and scenic harbor tours to a lively cultural festival and a firehouse cook-off, here’s what’s happening near you.

📚 LOS ANGELES LIBROS FESTIVAL
Saturday, September 26 | 10:00 AM-4:00 PM
Celebrate books, literacy and community at the Los Angeles Public Library’s free bilingual festival at Central Library. Enjoy Spanish-language and bilingual storytelling, musical performances, authors, workshops and books for the whole family. Registration is available through Eventbrite.
🌐 LAPL.org/libros

🛥️ FREE HARBOR BOAT TOURS
Saturday, September 26 | 11:00 AM–2:00 PM
Explore the Port of Los Angeles during a free, 50-minute narrated harbor tour departing every 30 minutes from Downtown Harbor in San Pedro. Boarding is first-come, first-served, and the line will close at 1:00 PM or when capacity is reached.
🌐 PortOfLosAngeles.org

🪅 LATINO CARNAVAL 2026
Saturday, September 26 | 11:00 AM–7:00 PM
Celebrate Latino culture at the free 2nd Annual Latino Carnaval at The Reef in South Los Angeles. The festival features live music across two stages, carnival rides and games, food, drinks and more than 200 vendors. Free advance RSVP is required.
🌐 Instagram: @CurrenDPriceJr

🚒 SALUTE TO FIREFIGHTERS FESTIVAL
Saturday, September 26 | 9:00 AM–4:00 PM
Celebrate Los Angeles firefighters at Warner Center Park in Woodland Hills. More than 15 firehouses and fire-service partners will compete in a cook-off. The free festival also features live music, a classic car show, a beer garden, firefighting demonstrations and family activities. Tasting passes are sold separately, with proceeds benefiting the Widows, Orphans & Disabled Firefighter’s Fund.
🌐 WODFF.org

title: LA’s Caribbean Heritage Festival 2026
description:
South Los Angeles came alive with vibrant music, delicious food, and cultural traditions as neighbors gathered for the annual Caribbean Heritage Festival. The celebration highlighted the rich heritage, shared history, and cultural connections between the Caribbean and African American communities.

Families enjoyed authentic Caribbean cuisine, traditional clothing, music, dancing, and activities for children. Attendees proudly represented countries from across the Caribbean region, including Belize, Trinidad and Tobago, Barbados, and Haiti. Beyond the festivities, the event celebrated cultural identity, resilience, and the importance of community representation.

Organizers hope to continue expanding the festival each year, with a long-term vision of bringing a large-scale Caribbean Carnival to Los Angeles, inspired by celebrated events in New York City and Toronto.

Though the City’s Urban Forestry program doesn’t plant palms, our team maintains more than 43,000 palm trees that currently exist across our neighborhoods. With appropriate funding, palms are pruned every two years to ensure the public's safety in the city right-of-way, and to support the health of the trees. 

Our tree maintenance teams will be servicing many neighborhoods throughout the city for Fiscal Year 2027, including Barrio Logan, Paradise Hills, University Heights, Encanto and North Park. To learn more about how we care for our urban forest, or to see our FY2027 palm tree pruning cycle schedule, visit: sandiego.gov/trees/maintenance.

title: Government Operations Committee - SAP  - 3/27/26
Budget Open House
description:
County residents gathered to learn more about the County’s $9.15 billion recommended budget at an Open House at the County Operations Center Thursday night.

County officials invited the public to come to the event to give them more information, and to let them pose questions and voice their opinions about the recommended budget that was released May 18.

The County also held a virtual Zoom meeting with the same information on Wednesday night, May 27, for people who could not attend Thursday’s open house.

The County Board of Supervisors is set to officially open the public hearing on the Recommended Budget at 5 p.m. Monday, June 1, and to deliberate and adopt a new budget June 25. To learn how to participate in Board meeting, whether by attending in person or watching online, go to the Clerk of the Board’s website.

Thursday evening’s open house was held inside and outside the Chambers at the County Operations Center with information for adults and even fun things to see for children.

The open house featured informational posters, tables manned by staff from County departments, a San Diego County Fire truck and ambulance, the County Department of Public Works first Electric Vehicle street sweeper, a County Library outreach van, and even a County Parks and Recreation “discovery table” where children could see and touch animal furs and learn about our local environment.

People learned more about what services the County provides, how the budget was created, where funding comes from, and were shown proposed numbers for budget priorities.

Those priorities included behavioral health, public safety, housing and homelessness, infrastructure, support for vulnerable populations and environmental sustainability.

title: City Council Meeting SAP - 1/20/26
Parking Changes at Balboa Park Starting March 2
description:
More free parking is now available in Balboa Park for City of San Diego residents, starting today! 

Make sure you verify your City of San Diego residency online ahead of time, and then you can access the free Resident Level 2 and 3 parking passes to park for FREE in 7 Balboa Park parking lots. The pass is available per vehicle and is valid for 3 years. There is a one-time $5 registration fee to cover the cost of processing the applications; this fee is not collected by the City. 

In premium (Level 1) parking lots, verified City residents qualify for half-off parking rates. Three hours of free parking is available for everyone at Lower Inspiration Point (including non-City residents), and there’s a free tram available to transport you to the center of Balboa Park. 

Verifying residency online requires you to upload a driver’s license, utility bill, property tax bill or rental agreement, and it may take a few business days to process, so plan ahead! Go to sandiego.thepermitportal.com. 

Balboa Park’s maintenance and operations are funded through the City of San Diego’s General Fund.

title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspection (SBC) May 7, 2026 Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) meeting of May 7, 2026 discussed recent in custody deaths, bringing the yearly total to 17. The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) reported on housing challenges, triple bunking, and pending autopsies but faced extensive commissioner concerns regarding sanitation, water quality, delayed medical care, inconsistent grievance procedures, Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) issues, and treatment of transgender individuals. Inspection reports across Men’s Central Jail (MCJ), Twin Towers Correctional Facility (TTCF), and Century Regional Detention Facility (CRDF) continued to show unsafe and unsanitary conditions.

The Commission approved minutes from previous meetings, advanced follow up work with the Civilian Oversight Commission and unanimously adopted a formal position supporting the closure of MCJ without a replacement facility. Additional motions addressed environmental hazards, jail death accountability, and protections for transgender and gender diverse people. The LASD was directed to provide several policies and data sets.

title: Upgrades Coming to Clairemont Pool!
description:
Upgrades are coming to the Clairemont Pool! 🏊 

The City is working hard to complete the ongoing renovation project at the Clairemont Pool so that the facility can reopen as quickly as possible. Significant improvements have already been completed, including replacement of the pool deck, new pool tile, lighting and electrical upgrades, a new boiler, and installation of the permanent fence posts.

Remaining fencing work is moving forward, and once complete, final plaster will follow, along with installation of the new pump and filtration system. 

The City is focused on completing the project and getting the Clairemont community back in the water as soon as possible. Clairemont Pool is currently anticipated to reopen in Spring 2027.

Residents can get ongoing project information on a dedicated Clairemont Pool Renovations webpage sandiego.gov/pools/clairemont-pool/renovations.

title: The Blue Notebook Review - Nov. 30 - Dec 6, 2025
description:
Ho Ho Ho! 🎄 The Blue Notebook Review is officially in the holiday spirit.

Sgt. Rick is back with a festive edition of the Blue Notebook Review, complete with seasonal décor brought to life with help from Cadet Alexis (minus the Charlie Brown tree — that one’s on Sgt. Rick).

Whether you celebrate Christmas, Hanukkah, Kwanzaa, Las Posadas, Winter Solstice, or simply the season itself, this episode reflects what this time of year is all about: community, service, and accountability.

This week’s highlights:

• 2,608 calls for service (115,880 YTD)
• 58 arrests | 18 encampments cleaned | 11 5150 holds
• Calls down 4.3%, arrests up 20.7% year-over-year
• Downtown livability operation and notable arrests
• Drone response safely resolves a “man with a gun” call
• 307 traffic stops focused on holiday safety

🎖️ Plus, a historic moment for SMPD — Chief Darrick Jacob is officially appointed, marking the first internal Chief promotion since 1979.

🐾 Holiday joy at the Animal Shelter, thanks to Warner Bros. Animation & DC Studios — and six pets adopted, with donations continuing next week.

It’s a busy season — and our favorite kind of busy.

This is your Blue Notebook Review.

title: Важное сообщение от DPSS о приостановке работы федерального правительства
description:
Если вы получаете пособия CalFresh, вы, вероятно, слышали о текущей приостановке работы федерального правительства и ее влиянии на ваши пособия CalFresh.

Вот что вам нужно знать:
• В связи с приостановкой работы федеральное правительство не будет предоставлять пособия CalFresh в ноябре 2025 года. 
• Как только приостановка работы завершится, пособия будут выданы тем, кто имел на них право в ноябре. 
• Если срок вашего полугодового отчета (SAR 7) или ежегодного продления приходится на период приостановки работы, вы ДОЛЖНЫ заполнить их вовремя, чтобы сохранить право на получение  пособий и продолжить получать их 
после окончания приостановки работы.
Мы рекомендуем вам посетить местный пункт раздачи продуктов питания и связаться с местными благотворительными организациями для получения помощи в это трудное время.

Список адресов можно найти на сайте LAFoodBank.org или позвонив по номеру 211, набрав 2-1-1, или посетив сайт www.211.org.

title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspection (SBC) June 9, 2026 Special Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission convened a special meeting to review recent detention facility inspections and address urgent environmental, safety, and operational issues in Los Angeles County jails.

Commissioners reported severe and recurring concerns across the Inmate Reception Center (IRC), Men's Central Jail (MCJ), and Century Regional Detention Facility (CRDF), including non functioning plumbing, unsafe water quality, unsanitary conditions, temperature extremes, delayed medical care, and inconsistent deputy compliance with body worn camera policies. Several inspections revealed significant barriers to accessing clean water, operational failures in showers and sinks, food contamination incidents, and reports of disrespectful or retaliatory treatment by staff.

The Commission approved the Report Back Pursuant to Board Motion the February 3, 2026 Board Motion: Water Quality and Safety at Century Regional Detention Center (CRDF) and Los Angeles County Jail Facilities to submit to the Board of Supervisors regarding water quality and hazardous conditions.

The meeting concluded with acknowledgment of three recent in custody deaths, with autopsies pending.

How LA Metro Plans to Move Millions for the 2028 Olympics
description:
Los Angeles is preparing to host the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with local leaders focused on keeping residents and visitors moving safely, efficiently and affordably.

To prepare for increased demand, LA Metro tested expanded service during recent major sporting events. According to Metro, the enhanced service supported more than 212,000 bus rides, while ridership on individual match days increased by 41% on the K Line and 23% on the C Line.

Officials are using lessons from these events to plan transit improvements for 2028 while addressing long-standing transportation needs. The goal is to make public transit a safer, more convenient and reliable option for residents, workers and visitors.

City and transportation leaders also hope these improvements will encourage more Angelenos to try public transit. Investments made for the Games are intended to strengthen the regional transportation network and benefit local communities long after 2028.

Los Angeles General Medical Center celebrated Hispanic Heritage Month by honoring Hispanic physicians, highlighting cultural representation in healthcare, and connecting patients, staff, and community members with valuable health and wellness resources.

title: San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria Elected President of the U.S. Conference of Mayors
description:
Mayor Todd Gloria has officially assumed the presidency of the United States Conference of Mayors after being elected by his fellow mayors during the organization's Annual Meeting in Long Beach. 

With his election, Mayor Gloria becomes the first Mayor from San Diego to serve as President of the U.S. Conference of Mayors and the first openly LGBTQ+ mayor elected to lead the organization in its history. 

“Though America’s mayors represent communities of every size and region, we share a common mission: delivering results that improve the lives of our residents,” said San Diego Mayor and U.S. Conference of Mayors President Todd Gloria. “At a time when too many families are struggling with the rising cost of living, mayors are focused on practical solutions. That starts with tackling the housing shortage, but also addressing public safety, economic opportunity and the quality-of-life issues residents care about most. Our job as mayors is to use our collective voice to advance solutions that make a real impact for our residents.”

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Foster youth are more likely to struggle academically and underperform in school than students outside of the foster system. The average high school student in San Diego County has a graduation rate of 87 percent, compared to 48 percent for foster youth.

To help change those outcomes, the Fostering Academic Success in Education (FASE) program was developed in partnership with County Child and Family Well Being, the Health and Human Services Agency, and the San Diego County Office of Education.

From Safe Parking Program to Home for the Holidays
description:
Home for the holidays. 🎁🏠 San Diego native Ashley and her kids moved into a new apartment this past October after experiencing homelessness and receiving help at the City's Safe Parking Program. Jewish Family Service of San Diego (JFS) operates the program, which aims to connect those living in their vehicles back into housing.

Ashley and her family stayed at the Rose Canyon site, where the City provides camper trailers for families. JFS helped her get her security guard license and she now works full-time supporting her family in their new home. 

Congratulations on the hard work and future milestones, Ashley! 🎉 

#sandiego

title: How to Get FREE Water for Your Garden in Los Angeles
description:
Get FREE recycled water for your Los Angeles garden, lawn, and plants! The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power offers this program to help residents save money. You can collect up to 300 gallons of non-potable water per visit to keep your landscape green during times of water scarcity.

Recycled water is perfect for irrigating trees, lawns, and vegetables. However, it is not safe for drinking or washing food. Simply bring your water bill to the fill station to complete a quick training session and start saving.

Visit the LA-Glendale Water Reclamation Plant on Fridays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. to receive quick training and start watering for free.

To learn more, visit: LADWP.com/RWFS

title: Virtual Public Workshop on Preservation & Progress Package A
description: Preservation and Progress is a comprehensive update to the City’s Heritage Preservation Program that aims to streamline review processes for new homes and other uses while continuing to protect places of historic, architectural, and cultural significance and encouraging their adaptive reuse. The initiative will be advanced in two parts—Package A and Package B. During this virtual workshop, City staff presented proposed updates to the Historic Preservation Element of the General Plan, revisions to the Historic Designation Appeal Process, amendments to the Complete Communities Housing Solutions Program, and a proposal to repurpose the existing Historic Preservation Fund to better support preservation work in underrepresented communities.

description:
A major warehouse fire that began in Boyle Heights on June 17, 2026, forced nearby businesses to close as smoke and unsafe air spread throughout the neighborhood.

More than a month later, local business owners and residents report ongoing health concerns, lost income, rats, flies, and persistent odors. Council District 14 Councilmember Ysabel Jurado and other City leaders are working to fast-track the cleanup and provide recovery assistance, while affected businesses seek additional support to reopen and bring customers back.

title: The Vision Theater Returns: South LA’s Cultural Crown Jewel
description:
A cultural jewel is coming to life in the heart of Leimert Park.

The City of Los Angeles has invested in the historic Vision Theatre, transforming it into a vibrant destination for music, dance, theater, and community gatherings. Featuring striking design and exceptional acoustics, the restored venue will showcase local talent while welcoming audiences from across Los Angeles and beyond.

Spearheaded by the Department of Cultural Affairs, the project honors Leimert Park’s enduring legacy as a center for Black arts and culture. The Vision Theatre will provide artists with a stage to share their work, strengthen connections throughout the community, and give South Los Angeles residents access to world-class performances close to home.

Every detail reflects the creativity and spirit of Leimert Park—and the community is ready for the world to experience it.

description: SAN DIEGO – On January 1, 2027, the City of San Diego’s minimum wage will rise from $17.75 to $18.35 per hour, but the raise only counts if it shows up in paychecks. This Thursday, October 8, San Diego City Councilmembers Marni von Wilpert and Sean Elo-Rivera will hold a press conference with workers, business owners, and community members to unveil their proposed amendments to the City of San Diego’s Earned Sick Leave and Minimum Wage Ordinance. The amendments would give the San Diego City Attorney the authority to pursue civil action against employers who commit wage theft and recover what workers are owed, including overtime pay.

title: Regular City Council - 04/22/98
Fall Connect Day Connects Angelenos With Help That Matters
description:
Community members gathered at St. Joseph Center for Fall Connect Day, a free resource event connecting individuals and families with services, information, and support.

Local organizations and government agencies worked side by side to help attendees access resources related to mental health, public benefits, housing, and other community needs. Participating partners included the Los Angeles County Department of Public Social Services, the Department of Mental Health, Council District 11, and community and corporate partners. Free haircuts were also available during the event.

St. Joseph Center provides a wide range of services for people experiencing homelessness and low-income residents, including outreach, housing assistance, benefits advocacy, case management, and connections to additional support.

Events like Fall Connect Day bring multiple resources together in one place, making it easier for community members to connect with services and organizations that may be able to help.

title: Los Angeles County Heat Action Plan Data Viewer Webinar
description:
Learn how to use the Los Angeles County Heat Action Plan (CHAP) Data Viewer to support heat resilience planning, grant applications, and project development. The LA County Chief Sustainability Office hosted this webinar in collaboration with the LA County Internal Services Department and the UCLA Luskin Center for Innovation on June 22, 2026. 

The webinar provides an overview of the CHAP Data Viewer, an interactive mapping tool that combines data on heat-related health burden, social vulnerability, community conditions and assets, and site-level heat data to help local governments, community-based organizations, and other practitioners better understand heat risk and identify potential resilience strategies.

To access the CHAP Data Viewer and related resources, visit: https://cso.lacounty.gov/ourcounty-plan/cso-current-initiatives/county-heat-action-plan/

title: Rent to a Veteran this Veteran's Day
description:
The County is encouraging landlords to rent to veterans holding a Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH) voucher. Hundreds of Veterans have vouchers in hand and need a place to stay.
 
Larry Neher’s father and his wife’s father served in the Navy and when a veteran applied to rent his Lemon Grove duplex, he was more than happy to support a fellow brother in arms. “It’s a great benefit. It’s helping out veterans, like we all want to try to do and thank them for their service,” he said.
 
Neher said payments are convenient, on time and there is nothing to worry about. He is one of over 375 landlords that currently partner with the County Housing Authority to provide a home to over 850 VASH Veterans. Landlords interested in giving back to those who have served and help them move forward are encouraged to submit an interest form.

title: World's Largest Swim Lesson!
description:
What a fun pool day! 🏊 

Last week, San Diego youth participated in the World’s Largest Swim Lesson at the Dr. Martin Luther King Swimming Pool. This global event helps communities build awareness about drowning prevention and the importance of teaching children to swim. 

The event also included a special water safety and drowning prevention proclamation with Councilmember Henry L. Foster III , Prevent Drowning Foundation of San Diego, American Red Cross Southern California Region, and the Independent Pool and Spa Service Association. 

Whether you're at the pool or the beach this summer, practicing water safety can help save lives. The City offers free, year-round swimming lessons emphasizing skill progression, water safety awareness and endurance.  

Learn more about swimming lessons and water safety tips🛟: sandiego.gov/pools/programs/swim-program 

#WaterSafety #DrowningPrevention #WLSL2026 #SanDiego

title: Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors Meeting - 9/1/26
description:
Remote Participation:
To address the Board, you are encouraged to register by visiting www.publiccomment.lacounty.gov; registration opens at 9:00 a.m. the day of the meeting:
- Complete the required fields - be sure to include your phone number if you are participating virtually
- Choose how you want to provide your comments (In-Person or Virtually)
- Select the agenda items that you want to comment on and whether you are For, Against, or Neutral on the item
- Select if you would like to receive text message reminders when your item is up for discussion
- Click Register
- Receive Confirmation e-mail

Call-In Instructions

To address the Board virtually during a live meeting, dial the conference line (213) 444-2600 using the telephone number that you provided during registration. Please note that using a different number may delay your access to speak.

Press * to access the menu and follow the prompts

LAPD Operation Firewall Press Conference 5/21/26
description:
Five counties in Southern California and 112 affiliate law enforcement agencies are uniting to protect local children from dangerous online predators. LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell announced the major regional crackdown alongside federal, state, and local partners in Operation Firewall. Key leaders included U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli, District Attorney Nathan Hochman, HSI Special Agent Eddy Wang, and Sheriff Don Barnes.

Law enforcement officers conducted undercover work and served warrants across five Southern California counties. The historic crackdown focused heavily on identifying predators on social media and gaming platforms. These collaborative efforts successfully rescued 40 children from abuse and resulted in 341 arrests. Social services like the Department of Children and Family Services immediately stepped in to provide trauma care to the victims.

This press conference highlights the impact of this operation.

title: The Future of California Ports: The First Hybrid Battery Electric Vessel
description:
A new era of sustainable maritime transportation has arrived at the Port of Los Angeles. ⚓🌊

Docked in Long Beach Harbor, the 108-foot passenger vessel El Escudo is redefining eco-friendly travel with its groundbreaking hybrid technology. Featuring the world's first parallel hybrid propulsion system, the vessel can operate on battery-electric power with zero emissions for hours at a time, helping reduce its environmental impact while delivering a smooth passenger experience.

Designed to accommodate up to 350 passengers, El Escudo is built for a wide range of activities, including harbor tours, whale-watching excursions, dining cruises, and ferry services. Combining innovation, sustainability, and comfort, this vessel represents the future of clean transportation on the water.

title: Los Ángeles Azules Make History in Panorama City
description:
Panorama City celebrated a major cultural milestone as internationally acclaimed cumbia group Los Ángeles Azules was honored with a permanent place in the community. The intersection of Van Nuys Boulevard and Chase Street was officially dedicated as Los Ángeles Azules Square, recognizing the group’s decades-long musical career and cultural impact.

For local residents, the dedication celebrates more than music. The new square highlights the cultural contributions of Los Angeles’ Latino communities and recognizes a gathering place in the heart of Panorama City.

The celebration brought music, dancing, and community together in the San Fernando Valley, creating a new public landmark where neighbors can gather, celebrate culture, and create memories.

title: Simple Steps to be Prepared for Emergencies
description:
Take simple steps that help keep you and your loved ones safe during emergencies. September is National Preparedness Month. 

Build a Kit: Gather essential supplies like water, non‑perishable food, medications, flashlights, and important documents.  

Make a Plan: Know where to go, who to contact, and how to stay connected. Talk with your family so everyone understands what to do if you’re separated or need to evacuate.

Stay Informed: Sign up for local alerts. Staying informed ensures you can respond quickly and confidently when emergencies arise.

For more information, visit sandiego.gov/oes/emergencypreparedness.

title: San Diego renews partnership with Caltrans to clear encampments
description:
Breaking through red tape + addressing unsafe encampments = success! Our agreement with Caltrans has been renewed for a second year to help people experiencing homelessness get off the streets and find help.  

Through this agreement, City crews can access Caltrans state property along freeways in the Downtown area to remove trash and waste. Since this effort began last year, more than 400 tons of waste has been removed. And, more importantly, 115 people have entered a sheltering program and 19 individuals have been housed.  

Caltrans is reimbursing the City up to $400,000 for maintenance along state right-of-way within this five-mile stretch of downtown. For more info, including how this year's crews can remove graffiti and brush in these areas, visit insidesandiego.org/city-san-diego-and-caltrans-mark-one-year-successful-partnership-and-renews-agreement-address

title: What Does Balboa Park's Future Look Like?

Calling all Balboa Park lovers! 💗  We want your input to help shape the park’s future.

We’re launching the first comprehensive update to the Balboa Park Master Plan since 1989, and community feedback is a key part of the process. Take the initial survey and let us know your thoughts on how the park should grow, connect to neighborhoods and best serve everyone who enjoys it.

مواردی که باید بدانید:
• این تعطیلی به این معناست که دولت فدرال،‌ مزایای برنامه CalFresh برای ماه نوامبر 2025 را صادر نخواهد کرد. 
• پس از پایان تعطیلی دولت،‌ مزایا برای افرادی که در ماه نوامبر واجد شرایط بوده‌اند،‌ پرداخت خواهد شد. 
• چنانچه موعد گزارش نیم‌سالانه SAR7 یا تمدید سالانه CalFresh شما در زمان این تعطیلی فرا برسد،‌ حتماً‌ باید آن را به موقع تکمیل کنید تا واجد شرایط باقی بمانید و بتوانید پس از پایان تعطیلی همچنان مزایای خود را دریافت کنید. 
توصیه می‌کنیم تا در این دوران دشوار، برای دریافت کمک، از مراکز توزیع مواد غذایی منطقه‌ای خود بازدید کنید و با سازمان‌های امدادرسانی متقابل محلی در ارتباط باشید. 

برای مشاهده فهرست این مکان‌ها،‌ لطفاً‌ به تارنمای LAFoodBank.org مراجعه کنید یا با شماره‌گیری
 2-1-1 با شماره 211 تماس بگیرید و یا به تارنمای www.211.org مراجعه کنید.

title: County Brings Community Together to Advance Food Justice Efforts
description:
Food is a basic need for people’s health and wellness, and it reflects our cultural identity. On Tuesday, March 10, the County brought together community members and partners that work across the food system to talk about ways the County can improve food access and reduce food insecurity. County staff shared updates on the 11 actions included in the Food Justice Community Action Plan, and invited participants to share ideas that can help shape what comes next.
 
Participants engaged directly with County staff leading the work as part of an interactive gallery walk, where they explored posters highlighting progress across the actions; and also had small group discussions ideas and perspectives on several key food access topics and discussed possible strategies moving forward. Input will help shape the County’s next steps and will contribute to an update that will be shared with the Board in Summer 2026. To learn more about the Food Justice Community Action Plan and stay involved, visit https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/food-justice-community-action-plan

title: A Love Letter to the Valley: Inside the San Fernando Valley’s 818 Day Festival
description:
Valley pride took center stage as Winnetka celebrated 818 Day at Cupid’s Hot Dogs. Bringing together live music, local artisans, and community nonprofits, the event showcased the deep-rooted pride and history of the West San Fernando Valley.

For 80 years, Cupid’s Hot Dogs has been a beloved third-generation family institution, serving classic eats while preserving its original atmosphere. Beyond the festivities, the day underscored a vital message: supporting historic mom-and-pop businesses is essential to keeping local neighborhoods healthy, resilient, and thriving.

With great music, delicious local food, and family fun, this year's 818 Day proved that Valley pride is stronger than ever. 

#LACityResidents

title: City of San Diego Offers Resources to Individuals Experiencing Homelessness
description:
The City continues hosting outreach events to connect individuals experiencing homelessness with a variety of services and resources – including support for their furry companions!

Pets are an important part of many people’s lives, which is why we’re grateful to community partners Project Street Vet, Spay Neuter Action Program and A New Life Rescue for joining us in providing critical pet services. Last week’s event was held in the Midway District.

Through these outreach events, individuals experiencing homelessness have direct access to important resources for both them and their pets all in one place.

Thank you to our community partners for collaborating with the City of San Diego to provide these resources!

title: We are busy planting trees!
description:
We're busy planting trees!🌳Today, students from Oak Park Elementary joined the Mayor, City employees and volunteers to plant 30 new trees at Oak Park Neighborhood Park.

The event is held every year around Nov. 8, Kate Sessions’ birthday, to honor the pioneering horticulturist known as the 'Mother of Balboa Park' for transforming San Diego with trees and gardens

Together, we're growing a green San Diego, one tree at a time. 💚 Happy Birthday, Kate. This is for you.

 #KateSessionsDay #SanDiegoAtWork #trees

title: Regular City Council - 2/25/26
Blue Notebook Review
description:
Get ready for another deep dive into community safety with the latest Blue Notebook Review! 

Sergeant Rick and the Neighborhood Resource Officers (NROs) are back with the essential stats and stories you need to know to stay informed about Santa Monica.

This episode features a mix of updates and community-focused reporting:

🤧 A Call for Help: Sergeant Rick is still battling a persistent cough! If you have any tried-and-true home remedies, drop them in the comments to help him out.

🛑 Traffic Safety (Beat 4): Officer Pardo highlights a busy period for the team, including 335 traffic stops and 240 citations issued. She also shares an incident involving a car that got stuck in the sand—remember, the beach is not a parking structure!

🚨 Crime & Investigations (Beat 1): Officer Hollowell reports on citywide efforts resulting in 109 arrests. He provides critical updates on a road rage incident on 4th Street and a recent unprovoked assault on a postal worker.

📣Homeless Outreach (Beat 3): Officer Tago details the Homeless Liaison Program's work, including 189 radio calls and 15 arrests related to park safety and warrant enforcement.

🏘️Community Engagement: Officer Avila (Beat 2) is up to his usual shenanigans. Brandon, is that really you? 

Stick around for the blooper reel at the end to see the lighter side of the NRO team!

As Sergeant Verbeck says: "Think before you drink, because when you’re drinkin', you ain't thinkin'!"

Drive safe, stay sharp, and let’s keep our community strong!

#SantaMonica #PublicSafety #CommunityPolicing #BlueNotebookReview #SMPD

title: How to Recycle Your Christmas Tree!
description:
Now that the holidays are behind us, here’s a friendly reminder to either drop off your tree at one of the City’s 16 drop-off sites, or recycle it in your green bin. 🎄 

First, make sure to remove all décor, lights and stands. Recycling helps reduce the amount of waste going into the landfill. Plus, recycled trees and other organic materials can be converted into high-quality mulch and compost that residents can pick up for free and use to nourish their gardens.

To learn more, visit SDRecyclingWorks.com and select “Events & Workshops.”

title: Clear the Streets. Reclaim Our Neighborhoods Press Conference 8/6/26
description:
Abandoned and inoperable vehicles can create safety hazards, attract illegal dumping, and contribute to neighborhood blight. Now, Los Angeles City Council District 9 and the Los Angeles Department of Transportation are launching “Clear the Streets: Reclaim Our Neighborhoods,” a new campaign designed to help South LA residents identify and report problem vehicles.

The campaign will use billboards, posters, social media, and other educational materials to explain which vehicles may qualify for removal and how residents can report them. Vehicles may be eligible for enforcement if they have not moved for 72 hours, are inoperable or unregistered, block traffic lanes, sidewalks, fire hydrants or driveways, or pose a public or environmental hazard.

During fiscal year 2025–26, LADOT removed 6,661 abandoned vehicles from streets across Los Angeles. Through this new partnership, CD9 will work with LADOT, parking enforcement, community organizations, and residents to identify recurring problem areas and improve coordination.

Report an abandoned or inoperable vehicle:

📞 CD9: 213-791-0362
📧 Email: cd9abandon@lacity.org
📞 Citywide hotline: 1-800-ABANDON (1-800-222-6366)
🕗 Monday through Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.

title: What is National Night Out?
description:
The City of Los Angeles and the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) bring residents, officers and City officials together for National Night Out. Held annually on the first Tuesday in August, this nationwide event provides a relaxed setting for Angelenos to meet local LAPD officers and connect with their neighbors.

See how National Night Out builds trust, strengthens relationships and helps create safer, more connected Los Angeles communities.

description: After the Eaton Fire swept through Altadena, the Black community there was faced with the loss of generational wealth, a cultural legacy and the bonds that tie neighborhoods together. title: This is where all your trash goes!
description:
Get a behind-the-scenes look at what happens to your curbside trash, recycling and organic waste! ♻️ 

Join us Saturday, June 13, from 8 a.m. to noon for the Miramar Greenery Open House, a free, family-friendly event. Enjoy hands-on activities, tours of Landfill and Greenery operations, grab compost & mulch, and meet our recycling mascot, Bonita Blue Bin. 

📢 What to Know Before You Go:  
The Miramar Greenery is on Convoy Street, north of Highway 52. 

All ages are welcome (participants under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian). 

Registration is not required but is helpful.  

All tour participants must sign a safety waiver before boarding the bus tour. 

A cover or tarp for any truck bed is required if loading compost/mulch.   

If vehicles are carrying any waste or items for disposal, standard Landfill fees apply. 

For details, directions, requirements and more, visit sandiego.gov/miramargreeneryopenhouse.

#CityofSanDiego #SanDiego #Recycle #MiramarGreeneryOpenHouse #SDGreeneryOpenHouse #MiramarGreeneryFreeCompost

El 16 de septiembre conmemora el Grito de Dolores, el llamado a la independencia realizado por Miguel Hidalgo en 1810. Anoche, los angelinos se reunieron en el Ayuntamiento de Los Ángeles para "El Grito": una celebración de música, cultura, comunidad y la tradicional ceremonia del toque de campana.
¡Viva México! ¡Viva Los Ángeles!

title: Stand Next to Life-Size Orcas at LA's Natural History Museum
description:
Come face-to-face with life-size orcas and explore more than 35 million fascinating treasures at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, the oldest and largest natural history museum on the West Coast.

From towering marine mammals and world-class natural history collections to the seasonal Butterfly Pavilion and dazzling Gem and Mineral Hall, the museum offers an unforgettable journey through the natural world. Visitors can experience the special Orca exhibit, featuring life-size replicas that reveal how these remarkable animals relate to humans, Indigenous communities, and the broader ocean ecosystem—while learning why orcas are actually the largest members of the dolphin family.

Whether you're interested in science, history, archaeology, or wildlife, the Natural History Museum offers something for visitors of all ages.

One man with gloves, trash bags, and a camera is inspiring residents to help clean Los Angeles.

Budget and Finance Committee - 1/20/26
City Advances Plan to Implement New State Law that Encourages More Homes Near Transit
description:
A new state law that encourages more homes near transit is set to take effect on July 1, and the City is working on a plan to implement it in a way that makes sense for San Diego. Community input will play a key role in shaping the plan. 

The law requires cities to approve certain housing projects within a half mile of qualifying transit stops. The City will phase implementation in certain areas — such as very high fire severity zones and areas impacted by sea level rise — which means it will not take effect on July 1. This provides additional time to develop a thoughtful plan tailored to San Diego’s unique needs. In some areas, the law will take effect immediately.

Learn more about the law, the City’s approach and how to stay updated on opportunities to provide feedback: insidesandiego.org/city-advances-plan-implement-new-state-law-encourages-more-homes-near-transit

They also received a monthly stipend and support services to help remove barriers to EMS careers.

title: The Blue Notebook on Route 66

Blue Notebook Review: Stats, Stops & Steaks

This week’s Blue Notebook Review has a little bit of everything: public safety updates, Route 66 celebrations, traffic enforcement, and… steak with the fire department. Because public safety partnerships come in many forms. Some are medium rare.

This week, SMPD responded to 2,753 calls for service, made 108 arrests, and continues to see a 75% increase in year-to-date arrests compared to this time last year.

We also celebrated 100 years of Route 66 on the Santa Monica Pier, joined community events across the city, connected with St. John’s personnel, supported animal shelter engagement, and took part in a memorial run.
Officer Tago also shared updates from the HLP Team including:
📞 223 radio calls
👮 207 self-initiated contacts
🚔 31 arrests
📝 29 citations
⛺ 5 encampments addressed

On the traffic side, officers conducted 279 stops, resulting in 163 citations.

Watch the full Blue Notebook Review for the weekly rundown and community highlights.

title: County Employees Give Back: CECO Grants Nearly $109K to Local Causes
description:
The San Diego County Employees’ Charitable Organization (CECO) awarded $108,940 in grants to 87 community programs and the CECO Employee Crisis Fund at the annual CECO Awards Ceremony. 

This year’s awards support a wide range of nonprofits—including health clinics, homeless service providers, youth and after-school programs, and other organizations serving San Diego County residents. More than 80 organizations attended CECO’s annual awards ceremony at the North Inland Live Well Center in Escondido to receive their grant checks

CECO has been the charitable arm of the County of San Diego since 1956 and strives to lend a hand to the community by way of grants to local nonprofit programs and assistance to employees and retirees in need. One hundred percent of donations made to CECO are distributed back to the community.

title: City Council Meeting SAP - 1/16/26
Why Does Los Angeles City Hall Glow Teal?
description:
Every September, Los Angeles City Hall is illuminated in teal in recognition of Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month. This annual tribute marks a decade of partnership with The Ovarian Cancer Circle, raising awareness and honoring those affected by ovarian cancer.

Inspired by Robin Babbini, The Ovarian Cancer Circle is dedicated to raising awareness, supporting survivors and families, and advocating for those impacted by the disease. The teal illumination serves as a powerful symbol of hope, remembrance, and community solidarity.

For ten years, the organization has worked alongside Los Angeles City leaders to amplify its message and bring greater awareness to communities across the city. The annual City Hall presentation reflects a shared commitment to education, advocacy, and support.

Advocates expressed their gratitude to Los Angeles City Councilmembers for a decade of continued partnership and support, while looking ahead to many more years of illuminating Los Angeles in teal and raising awareness about ovarian cancer.

title: The 31st Annual Central Avenue Jazz Festival
description:
Los Angeles celebrated 31 years of music, culture, and community at the Central Avenue Jazz Festival.

The free, family-friendly festival brought thousands of music lovers to Central Avenue for live jazz performances, food, art, cultural activities, and community resources.

From the early 1900s through the 1950s, Central Avenue became the heart of Los Angeles’ African American community and one of the city’s most important centers for jazz, R&B, business, and entertainment.

Today, the Central Avenue Jazz Festival celebrates that rich cultural and musical legacy along the historic corridor, including performances at the iconic Dunbar Hotel.

More than a music festival, the event brings generations together to honor Central Avenue’s past while celebrating the artists and community carrying its legacy forward.

Don’t miss the next Central Avenue Jazz Festival. Learn more at CentralAveJazzFest.com.

At the Los Angeles Sports and Entertainment Procurement Summit, local entrepreneurs connected with vital resources to secure major contracts. Attendees accessed financial programs and guidance on certifications, including dedicated support for minority- and women-owned companies.

The goal is to help small companies build strong foundations today so they can scale into thriving midsize businesses tomorrow. Even if you missed the event, opportunity is still knocking. title: First Look: Space Shuttle Endeavour in Its Vertical Launch Position
description:
Space Shuttle Endeavour is now standing in its iconic vertical launch position.

The awe-inspiring orbiter is being readied for its public opening on November 13, when visitors will experience Endeavour displayed in its dramatic 20-story vertical launch configuration inside the new Samuel Oschin Gallery at the California Science Center. Designed to spark curiosity and inspire future generations, the exhibit showcases every stage of Endeavour's remarkable journey into space while highlighting the science, engineering, and technology behind NASA's Space Shuttle Program.

The vision to display a retired space shuttle in its launch position began during the Science Center's planning in 1992. NASA officially awarded Endeavour to the California Science Center in 2011, and the shuttle arrived in Los Angeles in 2012, making its unforgettable journey through city streets from LAX before spending several years on horizontal display while the new gallery was built around it. 

The California Science Center expects the new exhibit to attract even more visitors from around the world, especially as Los Angeles prepares to host the 2028 Olympic Games.

The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, permanent home of Space Shuttle Endeavour, will soon be ready to launch, with an opening date set for November 13, 2026. 

Plan your visit https://californiasciencecenter.org/

title: County Animal Services Officers Rescue Bobcat
description:
Last week a bobcat was attempting to enter a fenced-in chicken coop in the Jamul area and got caught in the netting surrounding it, getting its feet caught up while trying to free itself.

The owner called County Animal Services to come and extricate the bobcat. The officers used blankets and a catchpole (for officer safety) to free the animal.

A healthy young bobcat, it had no injuries and was able to be released back into the wild after they cut the wiring that was tangled around its feet.
