These Hidden Facilities Keep Your Home Running
description:
Did you know your toilet, shower, laundry and kitchen sinks all go through our wastewater pump stations?

Our Public Utilities crews clean out wet wells and pumps a few times a week to keep systems moving, but it is up to everyone to keep trash out of the toilet. This includes "flushable" wipes, which take too long to break down and should be tossed in trash cans to avoid damage to household plumbing and our sewer system. 

When in doubt, throw it out. Thank you for doing your part! More information: sandiego.gov/public-utilities/customer-support/do-not-flush

title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) March 5, 2026 Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) meeting of March 5, 2026, reviewed current conditions, operational challenges, and inter agency coordination across Los Angeles County detention and justice facilities. There were updates from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD), Correctional Health Services (CHS), and the Department of Public Health (DPH), along with inspection findings from various facilities.

The SBC emphasized ongoing concerns related to in custody deaths, the need for consistent property transfer procedures, food service quality, Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and mental health follow up protocols, particularly regarding Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA)-   related referrals. The LASD reported progress on custodial facility contract renewals, food service modernization, and coordination with Health Services. The SBC examined gaps in water quality testing practices and requested improved interdepartmental reporting.

Facility inspections highlighted issues including outdated equipment, grievance form availability, disorganized property storage, and inconsistent documentation practices. While some facilities showed improvement, others required further follow up due to infrastructure problems or staff-related closures.

Action items assigned across agencies, focused on standardizing procedures, improving data reporting, and resolving facility specific deficiencies. Water quality reporting and special diet tracking—were continued to the next SBC meeting for comprehensive review.

title: Los Angeles Stands with Armenian and Russian Communities
description:
Local leaders and community members gathered at TUMO in North Hollywood for a panel discussion addressing the impact of discriminatory rhetoric on Armenian, Russian, and other immigrant communities.

The discussion focused on remarks made by federal official Dr. Mehmet Oz during a visit to Los Angeles and the economic harm reportedly experienced by nearby businesses, some of which saw sales decline by more than 30%.

Panelists emphasized the power of words, the importance of standing against hate and discrimination, and the City’s commitment to supporting immigrant communities. The conversation also explored potential legal avenues the City could pursue to help protect residents and businesses harmed by discriminatory statements or actions.

LAPD Swears In 25 Brave Teens Fighting Cancer as Honorary Officers
description:
Twenty-five children battling cancer received a special welcome at the Los Angeles Police Department’s Elysian Park Police Academy, where they became honorary officers for the day.

In partnership with the Sunshine Kids Foundation, LAPD hosted children from across the United States for its Junior Officer Day. Each child took part in a swearing-in ceremony and received a junior badge before being paired with an LAPD Reserve Officer for an interactive look at several specialized units.

The day included demonstrations and displays from LAPD Air Support, SWAT, the Metro Mounted Unit, Bomb K9, Dive Team, Bomb Squad, Motors, and Communications, giving the children an up-close look at different parts of the department.

The annual event is part of LAPD’s longstanding partnership with the Sunshine Kids Foundation, a nonprofit that provides free activities and emotional support for children undergoing cancer treatment. The day offered the children a chance to have fun, make memories, and connect with officers and other young people facing similar experiences.

title: Street Lighting Electrician Explains San Diego's Series Circuit
description:
Fixing our streetlights requires more than swapping out a bulb. There could be a range of issues to troubleshoot. Some of San Diego’s streetlights run on a series circuit, similar to Christmas lights. If one light goes out, the whole block could go dark. 

We have electricians working hard to identify the problems and fixing them as quickly as possible. The City uses parking meter funds on much-needed repairs and maintenance, like getting these streetlights back on again.

title: County Animal Services Rescues Small Dog Trapped in Storm Drain, Reunites Her with Owner
description:
County Animal Services rescued a small dog from a Spring Valley storm drain Monday after officers found her trapped and unable to climb out.

Animal control officers responded to the 600 block of Felicita Avenue in Spring Valley. Officer Myers climbed into the storm drain, used treats to coax the dog close, then lifted her to Lt. Raygosa at street level.

Staff brought her to the Bonita animal shelter, where she was cleaned, fed, vaccinated and checked for a microchip. Shelter staff said she appeared underweight, very hungry and had a dirty coat, suggesting she may have been lost for some time. 

Later that day, a woman arrived at the shelter reporting her dog, Teddy, had been missing for more than 30 days. She said her family had been searching extensively — posting flyers, driving the neighborhood daily and working with local dog rescuers.

Based on the information she provided, shelter staff confirmed the rescued dog was Teddy. While Teddy was initially withdrawn, she became alert the moment she saw her owner, wagging her tail and howling with joy. Her owner expressed deep gratitude for Teddy’s safe return and thanked staff for their help.

County Animal Services promotes the humane and responsible care of pets in the unincorporated areas of San Diego County. The department provides 24-hour animal rescues, supports residents who can no longer care for their pets, investigates and stops animal neglect and cruelty, enforces state and local laws, and educates the public about animal welfare, restraint and licensing.

South LA’s Vibrant Latino Carnaval
description:
South Los Angeles came as neighbors gathered to celebrate culture, history, and community at the District 9 Latino Carnival. Hosted by Councilman Curren Price for Latino Heritage Month, the outdoor festival brought families together across generations.

The festival grounds came alive with music, hands-on booths, youth games, and local craft vendors. Food lovers enjoyed an exciting mix of dishes, lining up for classic Mexican and Salvadoran specialties alongside trendy birria ramen. Families explored vibrant art displays and danced to upbeat tunes while connecting with neighbors and supporting local businesses.

By highlighting local heritage and talent, the carnival offered far more than simple fun. It built lasting neighborhood pride and created meaningful memories for South LA families.

title: "The World Wasn't Built for Us": LA’s Fight for Accessibility
description:
More than one million Los Angeles County residents live with a disability, underscoring the importance of making public programs, services, and spaces accessible to everyone.

The City of Los Angeles is updating its Citywide ADA Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan, reviewing City programs, services, activities, facilities, communications, policies, and digital resources to identify accessibility barriers and prioritize improvements.

As part of the process, residents and advocates have shared their experiences and accessibility priorities through a public hearing and community survey. That feedback will help the City identify areas for improvement and inform the updated Transition Plan.

Los Angeles residents are encouraged to share their experiences by completing the City’s ADA Public Input Survey at Disability.LACity.gov by October 30, 2026.

title: Inside Lincoln Heights' Massive 1,700 Backpack Giveaway
description:
Back-to-school shopping is tougher than ever, but Lincoln Heights isn't letting high prices hold students back. Council District 1 recently stepped up to host its third annual backpack giveaway, bringing massive relief to local families.

Volunteers handed out 1,700 brand-new backpacks stuffed with essential school supplies like notebooks and pencils. Dozens of local organizations joined the drive, connecting parents directly to vital housing and health services.

With rent and uniform costs soaring, the event aimed to lighten the heavy financial load before the first school bell rings. Beyond the supplies, the rally proved that community spirit is the ultimate weapon for student success.

Vision Theatre Ceremony & Celebration Grand Reopening 8/20/2026
description:
A historic Leimert Park landmark is stepping into a new era. Following a nearly $40 million restoration, the Vision Theatre has been transformed into a state-of-the-art, 729-seat performing arts center in the heart of South Los Angeles.

Originally opened in 1932 as the Leimert Theatre, the Art Deco venue was renamed the Vision Theatre after actress Marla Gibbs purchased it in 1990. Its restoration preserves historic features, including the auditorium’s ceiling mural, while adding modern production systems and ADA-accessible improvements.

The Vision Theatre will operate through a partnership between the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs and WACO Theater Center. Programming will showcase local, emerging, national, and international artists, along with community events, arts education, and City-partnered cultural programs.

The ribbon-cutting celebration honored the theater’s history and community legacy through land and labor acknowledgments, a libation ceremony, a blessing of the space, and performances by the Spirit Chorale of Los Angeles and Karen A. Clark.

WACO Theater Center’s grand opening is planned for November 2026, followed by the launch of its first full season in February 2027.

title: Bitten by a Rattlesnake? Every Second Counts
description:
What should you do if you encounter a rattlesnake? The Los Angeles Zoo and the Los Angeles Fire Department are sharing information about rattlesnakes.

While rattlesnakes are most active in the spring and summer, they are present year-round in Southern California because they are native to the Los Angeles area. When snakes have access to food, water, and shelter, they can settle nearby. To discourage them, keep garbage in secure containers to avoid attracting rodents, which in turn attract snakes. Also, seal any openings, as snakes can fit through holes as small as a quarter.

A rattlesnake’s signature rattle may not always be heard. They often stay quiet if they don’t feel detected and typically strike only when threatened. When outdoors, keep children within arm’s reach and dogs on a short leash. If you are bitten, call 911 immediately and treat it as a medical emergency.

title: Historic Filipinotown Comes Alive
description:
Historic Filipinotown came together at Unidad Park to celebrate community, culture, and connection at the one-year anniversary of the Kanto Corner HiFi Fall Fest.

Held quarterly in Los Angeles’ Historic Filipinotown, Kanto Corner brings neighbors together to celebrate Filipino heritage, support local businesses, and strengthen community ties amid concerns about displacement and gentrification.

Mutual aid was at the heart of the Fall Fest, with organizers partnering with neighborhood markets to distribute fresh groceries and connecting residents with health providers for free on-site services.

What started as a neighborhood gathering has grown into a welcoming space where immigrant families and longtime residents can connect, access resources, and celebrate the community they call home.

Following its spring and summer events, Kanto Corner returns to Historic Filipinotown this December for Winter Fest.

title: Pacific Palisades Farmers Market Reopens After Devastating Fires
description:
The Pacific Palisades Farmers Market is officially back home! Its grand reopening marks a major milestone in the neighborhood’s recovery following the devastating wildfires.

After nearly two years away, longtime vendors, residents and friends reunited to celebrate the return of a beloved community tradition. Founded 26 years ago as a grassroots neighborhood project, the weekly market has become an important gathering place where families shop, support local farmers and stay connected.

Although the market is currently operating at about half its original size, its return filled the community with hope and joy—and signaled another meaningful step forward for the Pacific Palisades.

Residents can once again shop for fresh produce and reconnect with neighbors every Wednesday beginning at 1:30 p.m. As one longtime farmer shared, when you plant a seed, extraordinary things can happen.
